#3869. Activision to remove Itaewon crowd crush footage from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and apologises to victims' families

"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims."

Activision has apologised to the bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it will remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

In a new statement reported by Inven Global, Activision said the footage "will be completely removed" via a game update scheduled to roll out on 12th November.

The statement was issued in Korean, and the quotes come via Inven Global's AI-assisted, editor-reviewed translation.

As we reported earlier this week, the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died. The bereaved families' association and the Citizens Countermeasure Meeting called for its removal.

"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims who were deeply hurt by this incident, as well as to everyone we have caused concern," Activision said.

The publisher also said that Modern Warfare 4 "is a work of fiction created to provide realistic immersion", and it "never intended to evoke or trivialise any tragic event, including the Itaewon crowd crush" by using real news broadcast footage.

The controversy has also reached the South Korean government. During a press briefing, minister of the interior and safety Yun Ho-jung described the footage's inclusion as "secondary harm", and said: "I believe appropriate sanctions should be imposed".

"Using such a tragedy as material for a game, a form of entertainment or business, is something that should be refrained from as a matter of human ethics," Yun added. He said it was up to the relevant agencies to decide "whether to impose punishment or block it to make general access difficult".

Activision's earlier statement to Eurogamer said the opening cinematic "utilises some real world news coverage to establish the game's fictional narrative", and was "not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form".

#3867. Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic's next DLC is set to expand the city building sim into the one place not corrupted by capitalism: SPACE

Following not the inherent liberal capitalistic framework of city builders like SimCity but instead a revolutionary (sorry) interpretation of planning and logistical simulation that prioritises centralisation and minute detail, Hooded Horse and 3DIVISION's Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic offers a tense, socialist look at what a citybuilder could be. Fellow contributor Sin Vega, in her 1.0 review, described it like this: "You have to build things to demolish things. That might be Workers & Resources in a nutshell. You're not managing budgets (money is exclusively for imports/exports), you're organising stuff." Now, having previously expanding out of the Soviet Republic and across the globe with the World Maps DLC, the next step for socialist citybuilding is, of course, space. Our Edwin outright predicted this two years ago, correctly calling that "the logical endgame here is to go to space." Good on him.

The Space Program DLC, set to release on November 23rd, will add a variety of new technologies and types of industry to the builder. It looks like it'll focus on not only the actual rockets that get into space, and the spectacle of it all, but also the huge amounts of science and industry that get to the point of rockets not exploding upon takeoff. For example, while it's all well and good for Space Program's scientists to be able to design rockets that are capable of remaining together for long enough to land safely, the designs they dream of still have to be built, meaning that industrial pipelines must be effectively centralised to ensure that every single component is of high quality and arriving in the required quantity.

The update also specifies the Sputnik and Vostok programs as elements of the expansion, implying a close historical aspect to it — though, elsewhere, "an unprecedented duel with nature" is mentioned, which is referring to either the simple harshness of space or aliens. Jury's out. A 1960s campaign will be a star feature of the DLC, which is described as a place for players to learn the new mechanics "in relative peace, surrounded by a happy, healthy, and economically stable utopia." What an idea.

Konami might have finally set down the Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol 1 to focus on releasing Metal Gear Solid 4 from its PS3 prison, but modders continue chipping away at the PS2-and-earlier era Metal Gear games. MGSHDFix, whose mission statement is to repair broken visual bugs, fix crashes, and generally give the older Metal Gears a bit of a spitshine, has got a big new update. Now is the era of MGSHDFix 5.0 (actually, 5.0.1. There was a hotfix).

"We've got performance improvements, massive vanilla loading time reductions for MGS2, loose .MP3/.WAV/.OGG/FLAC soundtrack loading for MG1/MG2, WIP raw mouse input support, and loads of new restoration and bugfixes", writes author Afevis Solmunko.

There are, to be honest, way too many fixes to properly delve into here, so I recommend either checking the patch notes out yourself or taking the mod for a spin in your preferred Metal Gear. We can call out some of the big ones, though.

For example, want to play Metal Gear 2 as Mel Gibson? No? Well that's a shame, bucko, because MGSHDFix 5.0 provides an option to restore that game's MSX2 sprites. "Yes, you can finally experience Mel Gibson fighting Sean Connery as Kojima intended," writes Solmunko.

Also in the OG MGs, there's now an option "to make doors automatically check your inventory for keycards (how MGS2 keycards work)", which frankly sounds blasphemous to me.

More practically, the latest version of the mod boasts that it dramatically cuts down loading times in MGS2. "We've greatly sped up level loading by adding a new system that prefetches a list of all the assets for all the rooms that are directly connected to the current stage you're in… Speedrunners have reported that this new prefetch system has shaved upwards to 5 minutes off of the elapsed realtime from their runs". On Linux (and thus, Steam Deck) specifically, Solmunko says this can "reduce level transitions load times by 4~6 seconds for every room you go into".

Plus, MGS2 and MGS3 now have limited support for raw mouse input in third-person, with support for first-person hopefully coming in MGSHDFix 5.1.0.

#3864. PUBG live-action series in the works at Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct and star

PUBG is being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Krafton announced the adaptation on 30th October, adding that Glover's brother Stephen, his writing partner on Atlanta, will join the project as a writer and executive producer.

The series will also be executive produced by Michael Schaefer for Neon TV, Fam Udeorji for Gilga, and Taeseok Jang and Sujin Lee for LV3H. LV3H is Krafton's entertainment arm, and it's involved in both developing and producing the show.

There's no word yet on a release window, plot, or who else will star.

Glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and says the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

Earlier this month, Krafton revealed it was ending development of PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction shooter spin-off announced nearly a year ago. The publisher’s other games include Subnautica and InZoi.

#3863. I'm sad that the Like A Dragon creator's new studio is closing, but I wish their now-cancelled debut Gang of Dragon wasn't just LAD again

Less than a year after the announcement of their first game, and only four years after the studio's creation, Gang of Dragon developers Nagoshi Studio have been dissolved by a shareholders' resolution (thanks, Gematsu.) That also means a premature end for Gang of Dragon, which was announced at last year's Game Awards with a flashy trailer featuring Like a Dragon-esque realistic visuals, combat and exploration through Kabukicho, a couple new elements like actual gunplay and car chases, as well as the star power of actor Ma Dong-seok (a.k.a. Don Lee). Following reports in March that NetEase, the studio's source of funding, would be pulling said funding in May due to ballooning costs reaching around seven billion yen, the time has sadly come for Nagoshi Studio, having not found any alternative funding sources in the time since.

Gang of Dragon looked very much to be 'just Like a Dragon again', which I find to be something of a depressing fate for a studio headed by the original series' creator. Having left Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio following Judgment and Yakuza: Like a Dragon, two of its most innovative games both with new protagonists and one entirely new turn-based gameplay style, it feels indicative of the industry that Nagoshi was granted funding seemingly on the condition that the studio makes something that just looks like the rest of the Like a Dragon series. I love Ma Dong-seok as an actor, but his presence was one of the more blatant, 'look, we got that guy!' castings of the LAD archetype, which is saying something considering Infinite Wealth had fucking Danny Trejo in a prominent role. The trailer closing with a shot of Dong-seok framed by Kabukicho's torii gate, maybe the most famous image from the Like a Dragon series, put a sour taste in my mouth as being just more of the same brand recognition (yet, for a new IP!) to prioritise safe return on investment.

I'm unfortunately not that surprised to see Gang of Dragon and Nagoshi Studio lost to time, though I am sad about it. I have some conflicted feelings on Nagoshi as a person/auteur, but I don't think he, or his studio, deserves to have funding pulled before they could even release anything as a result of NetEase deciding to pull investments out of non-Chinese companies over time. It's unknown what Nagoshi and the team will be attempting next, but I truly hope they can eventually make something. No More Heroes studio Grasshopper Manufacture was able to detach themselves from NetEase very recently and possibly avoid a similar fate, so it might not be impossible.

#3862. How to collect Nami’s Tangerines to help Sanji protect them in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

Fortnite’s Treasure Hunters season has quite a few different One Piece-themed missions available for you to tackle. One of the first ones you’ll encounter tasks you with collecting Nami’s Tangerines to help Sanji protect them.

The loot pool is massive, so figuring out how to find any specific item around the island can be tricky. If this task is giving you trouble, here’s how to collect Nami’s Tangerines to help Sanji protect them in Fortnite.

Nami’s Tangerines are a random loot drop item you can find just about anywhere on the island while looting. There is no specific, guaranteed way to find them, which means you instead have to regularly loot and hope you eventually come across them.

You have a chance of finding Nami’s Tangerines when opening any loot container you come across while exploring. This includes:

You can also find Nami’s Tangerines sitting on the ground anywhere around the island. They’re fairly common, so once you’re actively looking for them, finding the total amount required for this mission should be fairly easy.

Each time you come across Nami’s Tangerines, you’ll generally find more than one. Typically, they come in bundles of around three. This helps you progress through the mission associated with them much faster, as you need to find quite a few of them to get it done.

To complete the collect Nami’s Tangerines to help Sanji protect them quest, you need to find a total of 16 Nami’s Tangerines around the island. You don’t actually have to eat them; instead, you simply need to pick them up and have them in your inventory briefly for them to count toward this task.

You can find all 16 Nami’s Tangerines in one match or instead slowly work your way through this task across a few different ones. All that matters for this mission is that you eventually do manage to collect a total of 16 at some point before the season ends.

There are plenty of other missions you can find and work through around the island after checking this one off. "Just because you can upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models doesn't mean you should upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models."

Indie-oriented digital storefront Itch.io is beginning to push back against the rising flood of AI, announcing on social media that it's "deleted a couple terabytes of AI slop" and made it easier for users to filter out games made with generative AI.

A few days after Valve admitted that Steam has a problem with AI slop and game cloning, Itch.io chimed in to say it's experiencing something very similar: The number of game pages being created every day on the storefront has doubled over the past two months.

Itch.io didn't provide a reason for the phenomenon, but it's not hard to figure out: When one Bluesky asked why it was happening, Itch.io replied "take a guess," accompanied by crying and robot smilies, and then added that "the number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled."

Now it seems to be moving to action. "Just deleted a couple terabytes of AI slop," the storefront posted last night. "Just because you can upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models doesn't mean you should upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models."

The account also linked to Itch.io's guidelines on "uploading excessive amounts of automatically generated or AI-generated content," which says that while content created by generative AI "can be useful or interesting, do not use automated systems to mass produce product pages. We will consider this spam and may remove your pages from our browse and search pages."

The guidelines apply to, but are not limited to:

Like Steam, Itch.io requires developers and publishers to disclose their use of generative AI in their games. That disclosure requirement has now been expanded from game assets to "the tabletop (aka physical games), books, comics and soundtracks categories," all of which now require disclosure.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It has also added new browsing and search filters on the site, so users can exclude some or all use of generative AI.

The tabletop (aka physical games), books, comics and soundtracks categories on itchio now require completing an AI disclosure in order to edit or create your page. These join the game assets section which has required disclosure for the past 2 years.

The "No AI" tag page cuts straight to it:

Itch.io's action isn't likely to stem the tide of AI slop that's engulfing the world of gaming. Apart from the fact that it represents a very small percentage of a market dominated by Steam, the simple truth is that AI slop is easy to churn out in overwhelming quantities—that's what makes it so attractive to people who care less about creation than they do about making a few bucks on a lucky swing of the bat.

But it is action, and I think that's important: While some argue that mandatory AI disclosures have the potential to harm developers, the gen AI geyser is unquestionably doing harm right now, to users, developers, and the industry as a whole. Unless and until that changes, proactively excising the worst of the slop torrent and making it easier for gamers to avoid the mess entirely is the least that online storefronts can do.

Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition will launch on 12th November, bundled with a new mode called Dandori Academy.

Nintendo confirmed the date during yesterday's surprise Pikmin Day Direct, which also revealed that a demo will land on the Nintendo eShop on 2nd November. Any progress you make in the demo will transfer to the full game if you buy it.

Dandori Academy is a timed exam mode. The Direct showed off one of its exams, Gargantuan Garden, which challenges players to collect gold nuggets before time runs out (thanks, Insider Gaming).

The Switch 2 Edition will also let you give voice commands to Oatchi, the game’s dog companion. If you already own Pikmin 4 on the original Switch, you can buy an upgrade pack from the eShop.

Nintendo had warned ahead of the broadcast that there would be no new game announcements. Instead, Shigeru Miyamoto introduced Japanese actor Fuka Koshiba as a new ambassador for the series, and Nintendo confirmed that 1st November, today, is now Pikmin Day.

Pikmin 4 originally launched on Switch in July 2023. The Switch 2 Edition is one of two big Nintendo releases this month, alongside The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on 5th November.

#3859. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake review – Remasterpiece

An all-time classic reborn respectfully and beautifully.

I’ve talked in the past about how I’m not particularly a fan of the Zelda games, but it’s mostly because I’ve just never really dived into them, especially the latest open-world ones. But for Ocarina of Time, I’ve dabbled many times before and always respected it for how much it’s loved, even if I never could quite grasp the excitement myself.

As a kid, I remembered feeling overwhelmed and annoyed with the game’s controls (especially on that cumbersome Nintendo 64 controller) and muddy framerate that even then made it feel like a slog. Thankfully, with the newest version for Nintendo Switch 2, all of those issues have been assuaged to create a genuine masterpiece, reborn for modern-day gamers.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is genuinely one of the best games I’ve ever played, and one that I think all players of all ages should experience, whether they’re a hardcore fan of the original or a newcomer going in with zero knowledge. It’s just that good.

It all starts with a boy in the forest, a chosen one of sorts, who is shockingly thrust into an exciting, adorable journey to meet a princess and save the world. From there, from what I’ve gathered, it’s the same timeless story you remember from 1998. I venture to guess that long-time fans of this game will have a very emotional experience reliving it

At its heart, Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is what I would call a respectful remake/remaster, even if many will probably feel like Nintendo played it a bit too safe this time around. The changes made here have been minimal, focusing on quality-of-life improvements like the game’s controls, visuals, and sound, to enhance the experience without changing it very much at all.

Remakes are always a tricky task, because you need to maintain the allure of the original while also making it worthwhile to play a second time around. There’s been two kinds of remakes in recent years: games like Resident Evil 4 or Final Fantasy VII, which reshape the story and gameplay in numerous ways, or Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater and Demon’s Souls, which stay very true to the original, while focusing more on modernization and quality-of-life. Ocarina of Time definitely falls into the latter.

At the outset, the beauty of modern tech and the Switch 2’s hardware is on full display, boasting some of the best visuals the new console has released yet, especially when it comes to adding details that were not possible on N64: interiors look different thanks to no longer being flat polygons, Link’s tunics have awesome designs in the fabric, and even change color when it gets wet. And then there’s little things, how Link’s mouth subtly opens when taking a breath between notes on the Ocarina (you can also play the songs in the game by humming into your Switch 2, which is just plain cool).

It’s all incredibly detailed and gorgeous, and it’s locked at a rock-solid 60 FPS throughout, creating a smooth experience that we could’ve only ever dreamed of when dealing with the 20-FPS slog the original game offered.

Putting another of my complaints about the original to rest, the controls have been reimagined for modern games and gamers, and are incredibly well optimized for the Switch 2, especially when it comes to the Pro Controller (my preferred method whenever possible). Link can now sprint, and there’s a dedicated button for jumping, making platforming sections a joy. And yes, even the Water Temple is way better now, with the ability to quickly equip and unequip the Iron Boots by pressing down on the D-pad.

The hero can now also target foes with the ZL button and lock onto them when close, making combat a breeze, and maybe even a bit too easy, with nary a real challenge in my 25-plus hours in a first run, even with the game’s awesome and memorable boss fights. I couldn’t help but feel a bit of the adventure’s age here, so it would’ve been cool to see the combat maybe tweaked a bit to bring more of a challenge, but I don’t think it’s a huge deal either way.

This still feels like a masterclass in level design and gradual progression, all these years later. There’s no XP to earn, no checklists, just gradually getting stronger and unlocking new items to help you reach new heights on your journey, with some minor side quests to get into along the way.

Other additions to the adventure for 2026 include Threads of Time, which is a tapestry that weaves Link’s story as you play it, but also serves as a bit of a quest log if you don’t know where to go next. This is very helpful considering there are a ton of side quests, collectibles, and minor interactions to find both in the open world and dungeons you must conquer.

You can easily learn where to go or what to do by talking to NPCs around the vast kingdom of Hyrule, but the tapestry will occasionally update with an objective that you can finish (or not) by gently pushing you in a direction. For me, it was nice to have, considering I don’t remember much about the original game.

There’s also the Hall of Fallen Foes, which is a menagerie of enemies you’ve defeated that you unlock in the later stages of the game. It serves as something of a museum, allowing to to walk around and view the models of monsters and enemies you’ve taken down, but also do battle with them again to reprise the boss fights at your leisure.

The other main difference in this version of the game is the addition of voice acting in certain cutscenes. Many of the game’s conversations are done through text dialogue, but big story beats are voice-acted by a number of important characters like Navi, the Great Deku Tree, Zelda, and of course, Ganon. Everyone here sounds great, which is easy for me to say because I haven’t had my own version of their voices in my head for a few decades like long-time fans will. But don’t worry, the silent protagonist stays silent here, too, other than his classic grunts and exclamations while exerting himself.

The changes made to Ocarina of Time feel meaningful and worthwhile, and they do nothing to detract from the original game’s legendary experience. Instead, they enhance it in every way, making an unforgettable journey more accessible and fun than it ever has been.

I got a little emotional while playing OoT on Switch 2, especially when using the Ocarina to travel to and from the past. How jealous I am of Link’s ability to travel back in time. Like Link, I first entered the Temple of Time as a child and returned as an adult. Much has changed in the 28 years since the original was released, but the charm of this game is still there, and it feels prevalent throughout, even with a “modern” art style and rerecorded musical score.

I will leave a word of warning, however: make multiple saves before heading to the last areas of the game to take on the final boss, if you want to reach 100 percent completion and take on all the game has to offer. There’s no New Game Plus option, and no real option to go back and complete things if you don’t have a separate file ready to go (I’d be happy to find out I missed something if I’m wrong here).

I’d like to close with saying that, in my professional life as a journalist and critic, I’ve always felt hesitant to give out a score like this. It’s not perfect (nothing and no game is), but I’m confident that this is the one game to break that personal barrier with. Ocarina of Time is a legendary experience for a reason, and this remake is one of the best of its kind I’ve played yet. I’m hopeful that longtime fans will enjoy it, and I know that newcomers will find a lot of fun in the franchise if they’re diving in for the first time.

#3858. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel teaser all but confirms Hammerfell setting and means we can finally stop using that eight year old header image with the hills

Say hello to sandy scroll screengrab for the foreseeable future

Praise Talos and whatever other Elder Scrolls deities you might worship. We here at RPS and in the wider gaming press finally have new material to use when hunting for images to symbolise The Elder Scrolls 6. No more will we be limited to that shot of some hills from the 2018 teaser, because Bethesda have shown off an elder scroll covered in sand while revealing the new game's subtitle and all but locking in a setting. As a recent report from The Verge claimed, it's called The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel and looks to be set in Hammerfell.

These details were revealed in a short teaser at the end of a Todd Howard-fronted video celebrating Bethesda Game Studios' 40th anniversary. As such, the majority of the video is the Toddinator recapping the studio's history by touching on each of the games they've put out since 1986's Gridiron. Then, he looks to the future. "You know, everybody’s always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," the Toddfather said. "And we thought, hey, given the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called."

Cue a shot of an elder scroll buried in sand, followed by the The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel in fancy logo font. Then, a quote attributed to a moth priest called Yazar. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate." OOH, CRYPTIC. In all seriousness, between the subtitle, the sand, and Yazar being referred to as a moth priest in service of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, the Verge report's assertion that the game will be set in Hammerfell is essentially set in stone by this teaser even if his Toddliness didn't spell it out himself.

Sentinel's the name of both a kingdom and city in the Redguards' province. The inclusion of an elder scroll in the teaser and the quote from Yazar also lend credence to the Verge report's claim that the game will make a big thing out of unravelling secrets linked to the provenance of these mysterious bits of paper. As for the quote's yammering of lost futures and undone victories, I'll venture to speculate that it could turn out to be reference to the player character thwarting a Thalmor victory, since Skyrim seemed to set up the elves as being on the verge of conquering Tamriel as the Cyrodillic empire fractured and fell.

That may or may not be the case, but we do know for sure that this teaser likely means a huge downturn in use of the header image below. It's eight years old, pulled from The Elder Scrolls 6's infamous 2018 teaser. All these years on, the game's finally on the way. You've served us well, screengrab of some hills. Talos guide you to wherever less regularly used images go.

Elder Scrolls teasing aside, it's worth bearing in mind that Bethesda parent company Microsoft have spent the majority of this year gutting their workforce with mass layoffs and studio ditching. Microsoft are also still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#3857. Dune: Awakening's free Blood and Ice expansion swaps sand for snow on 1st December

Funcom's survival MMO Dune: Awakening is heading north with a free expansion that trades the deserts of Arrakis for a frozen new map.

The expansion, called Blood and Ice, will release on 1st December. Funcom said it adds "around 35 hours of new progression", along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialisation traits. It's coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox.

The new map, called the Polar Sink, turns the game's usual survival loop upside down. Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm, upgrading your gear with resources found only in the Polar Sink.

The map is split into two biomes, the tundra and the ice cap. You'll start in the tundra, where wealthy water shipper families have built lavish strongholds, before trying to get into the heavily guarded ice cap. Once you're in, you can harvest ice to cool your base equipment and speed up production.

According to Funcom, the expansion "brings the focus back to ground-level survival, with traversal, temperature management, and combat all playing important roles in your progression". The studio also said future updates will add more reasons to go back to the region.

Blood and Ice also brings a new Events tab to the main menu. Shortly after the expansion launches, a new event called Water Crisis will follow the current one, The Scourge. Funcom says every event can be completed in both single-player and multiplayer, and that it plans to run them more often, each with new stories and free rewards.

Funcom has also launched a cosmetics store, which it says will help fund continued development and free updates. The store will start with a rotating selection of items, including looks taken from the Dune films to coincide with Dune: Part Three's release in cinemas this December. The plan is to eventually make the full catalogue available at all times.

Several of the community's most-requested features are also on the way. Offline single-player is due this month, and from January 2027 you'll be able to copy characters from multiplayer servers to single-player, and from single-player to select private or self-hosted servers on PC. Full cross-play will also arrive in January 2027.

"We're far from done," Funcom said, adding that it has "ambitious plans for the year ahead", including major free updates in 2027. The studio says more than a million new players have joined since the game launched on consoles, alongside a rebuilt endgame, three DLCs, and the conclusion of the game's first story arc, Book One.

Just a couple of weeks ago, Norwegian developer Funcom, creator of Dune: Awakening and Conan Exiles - and many other games - confirmed it was entering a period of restructuring and bracing for layoffs as a result. You may remember the company making a similar move this time last year, months after the initial PC release of Dune: Awakening.

This week, Bethesda Game Studios is celebrating its 40th birthday—a celebration that included the full name reveal of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, successfully completing the eight-year task of adding a word to a thing.

In addition, Bethesda is commemorating the occasion with the launch of a 40th anniversary site collecting the anecdotes and favorite memories of studio staff, including one Alan Nanes. Now a design director, Nanes was originally hired at Bethesda as one of its first full-time QA testers—and by his own description, he got the job by being a pleasant fellow to spend time with.

According to Nanes, his history with Bethesda started during Morrowind's development. He was close friends with Bethesda devs in multiple departments, and it was an era where that was enough to get you in the building.

"Things were a bit 'Wild West' back then, and my friends allowed me to hang out (yes, before I was an employee) there, playing multiplayer games with them and just getting to know everyone," Nanes wrote. "Eventually, Todd Howard noticed my presence in the studio and asked if I wanted to test out their new game."

In time, his impromptu testing sessions started attracting an audience of Bethesda developers who would pick his brain about their design choices, scribble notes, and debate with each other about potential tweaks to the game while watching over his shoulder.

"It was an extraordinary feeling, the first time I felt like I was contributing to the creation of an actual videogame (I believe you can find my name in the Morrowind manual's credits under 'Special Thanks')," Nanes said. "After this became a regular occurrence, Todd Howard and Ashley Cheng seemed to decide having full-time, in-studio QA would be a valuable addition to the team, and I took on that mantle."

Nanes later graduated to a quest designer position for Oblivion, and was more recently credited as lead companions designer on Starfield. But while his tenure at Bethesda might've had a storybook trajectory, the history of QA workers at the studio has been a contentious one in the years since Nanes was hired.

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

Driven by frustrations surrounding compensation, advancement opportunities, workload, and more, QA workers at Bethesda's parent company ZeniMax initiated a unionization vote in 2022, officially forming ZeniMax Workers United - CWA—then the largest videogame union in the US—when the vote succeeded in January 2023.

Those frustrations remained unaddressed as contract negotiations with Microsoft stalled for over two years, driving the QA union to vote overwhelmingly in favor of authorizing a strike in April 2025. Its contract was ultimately ratified in June 2025. When a number of those QA workers were affected by Xbox's July 2026 layoffs, that contract allowed the union to enter into an "effects bargaining" process to negotiate severance terms for its impacted members, culminating in "a significant agreement" in September 2026.

#3855. How to get Captain X rewards in Fortnite Treasure Hunters

There are many unique skins you can unlock in Fortnite Treasure Hunters. One of the toughest ones to get your hands on is Captain X, a battle pass Outfit that requires quite a bit of progression to obtain.

This style will only be around and available to earn through quests in this season, so if you’re interested in adding it to your collection, you’ve got to get to work on it fast. Since Treasure Hunters is a mini-season, you’ve got quite a limited amount of time to work on it, so here’s how to get Captain X and all of his rewards in Fortnite.

Captain X is the grand prize in the Captain X rewards series, which means you must fully work through this special set of missions to earn him. To progress in this series, you need to complete varying amounts of weekly tasks. A total of 24 weekly quests must be finished to unlock him.

While there are lots of free rewards up for grabs this season, like Solid Gold A$AP Rocky and other rewards in the Pirate Chest, Captain X is not one of them. He is a battle pass-only outfit, which means you must have this pass unlocked to progress toward earning him.

Captain X also cannot be unlocked early on in the season, as there aren’t enough missions available to complete for him. He won’t be obtainable until Nov. 21, close to the very end of Treasure Hunters.

To ensure you’re able to get him, though, you’ll want to keep on top of completing as many weekly quests as possible leading up to his unlock date. Fresh missions are added every week, and checking off as many of them as possible will ensure you’re able to unlock Captain X and all of his associated prizes as soon as it’s possible to do so.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

In total, there are seven rewards available to unlock in the Captain X series. This includes the Captain X Outfit, various key accessory items designed to go with him, and a few other miscellaneous prizes. Here are all of the available Captain X rewards you can get.

There are plenty of quests you can work on to help you get closer to unlocking Captain X. Some missions you may consider tackling next include collecting Nami’s Tangerines to help Sanji protect them, contacting Slone on the Slone Phone in Plunder Port, and using Sprite Wanted Posters to dig up and open Sprite Chests.

#3854. Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3 has been announced, marking another attempt at a free-to-play team game after Gundam Evolution's unfortunate fate

Bandai Namco have released the initial announcement trailer for Mobile Suit Gundam Battle Operation 3, a free-to-play team action game and a sequel to 2018's Battle Operation 2. The trailer is very, very pretty, showing off Gundam units clashing in large-scale battles and infantry fighting beneath the colossal mechas' feet (kinda like Titanfall, in having both human and mecha players in the same match). I'm sadly not yet enough of a true Gundam fan to recognise many of these units on sight other than the RX-78-2, but there's a real variety shown off here.

MOBILE SUIT GUNDAM GUNDAM BATTLE OPERATION 3　Announcement Trailer Watch on YouTube

While there's no release date specified in the trailer, Bandai Namco have confirmed that there will be a network test in Japan through November 20th-22nd, with an open network test planned for the future (thanks, Gematsu).

Following the fate of Gundam Evolution, a 2022 attempt at a hero shooter featuring Gundam units, it's nice to see another shot at taking the Gundam series into a team format. Evolution suffered from the all-too-common trappings of heavy microtransaction inclusion, with several playable Gundam units with unique abilities only available through paying real cash. It was rightly criticised for this, and since Bandai Namco seemed to have had high hopes for the revenue it could make from said microtransactions, the lack of money made meant it shut down just a year later.

Contrastingly, from what I can see, Gundam Battle Operation 2 was received fairly well on its release. While little is actually known about the third game at this point, let's hope it has a better chance than the series' last big release. I will quickly note that the trailer does close with a "*Some content may require purchase" note, so it'll likely have some form of microtransaction in itself — hopefully not to the same degree as Evolution. And, while we're on the topic of Gundam, there's also 2027's Gundam Rogue Orbit, a drastically different game that seems closer to a Devil May Cry-esque action title (though, unlike Battle Operation 3, will begin life as a timed exclusive to PS5). Now, if we could get a Gundam game that plays something like Armored Core, and god willing a proper PC release, I would be a very happy girl.

#3853. Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online

Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online.

The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake".

Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload. There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style.

Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment.

Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats.

How do you solve a problem like Persona 4? At Gamescom, we sat down with series director Kazuhisa Wada to talk about the Persona 4 Remake, and ask about how Atlus is approaching the original text for the remake.

You might be thinking, if you're the optimistic sort, that today's official unveiling of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel means that wheels are turning and things are happening and you're going to be off to Hammerfell soon—or at the very least, learning more about what's coming in Bethesda's next big RPG. Alas, in a follow-up post on social media, the studio made it clear that you shouldn't start holding your breath just yet.

"Thank you for 40 years of shared memories," Bethesda wrote. "We can't wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it'll be some time before we're ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you."

Thank you for 40 years of shared memories. We can’t wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it’ll be some time before we’re ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you.

"Some time" is obviously not a defined span, but I find that generally speaking it's a nicer, more politic way of saying "long time"—for instance, you could say it's been "some time" since Bethesda first announced the Elder Scrolls 6, and yeah, that's true. It was also eight freakin' years ago, and we've heard basically nothing since.

That is, very roughly, the same amount of time Bethesda needed to make the first Elder Scrolls game, Arena, as well as Daggerfall, Morrowind, the Morrowind expansions Tribunal and Bloodmoon, and the spinoff games Battlespire and Redguard. If you're (relatively) new to the series, eight years represents the span between Oblivion and The Elder Scrolls Online, a stretch interspersed by Skyrim and five major expansions: Knights of the Nine and Shivering Isles for Oblivion, and Dawnguard, Hearthfire, and Dragonborn for Skyrim.

Of course, Bethesda's had other things on the go over the past eight years too. Todd Howard said shortly after The Elder Scrolls 6 reveal that it was in pre-production, while Starfield was in full production. Starfield was Bethesda's top priority in the years leading up to its 2023 release; Howard later said that they'd just wanted to answer the fan question (are you making a new Elder Scrolls?) that came up every time they announced something else, like Starfield.

"Just pretend we didn't announce it," he joked. "Doesn't exist. No one's heard a word."How long Sentinel will take to get from here to launch is anybody's guess, although Bloomberg's Jason Schreier said on Bluesky that it's "still more than two years away." When questioned about his prediction, Schreier asserted that it's not a prediction at all, and that he knows "the time frame the game is targeting."

#3851. How to get free AHA Advocate ID Card and Badge in Phasmophobia

There are lots of ways you can customize your experience in Phasmophobia, including an array of ID Cards and Badges you can equip to highlight various achievements and events. Sometimes, these special items are given away to all players, as is the case with the AHA Advocate ID Card and Badge.

ID Cards and Badges are some of the rarest and toughest items to unlock, as many of them require you to sink lots of time into checking off lengthy, complex goals. Because of this, free, easy-to-grab ones are always rather exciting additions you won’t want to miss out on, so here’s how to get the AHA Advocate ID Card and Badge in Phasmophobia.

You can unlock the AHA Advocate ID Card and Badge by logging onto Phasmophobia anytime during the redemption period. This is a free reward granted to all members of the community in celebration of over $200,000 being raised during Phasmophobia’s fundraiser for the American Heart Association Liive.

There are no additional steps you need to take to obtain this item, which is unusual for earning ID Cards and Badges, so it can take a bit of getting used to. Simply boot up the game, visit the board in the lobby, and select the “Accept” option on the AHA Advocate pop-up anytime before Nov. 15 to claim this reward and have it added to your collection forever.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Once you’ve got the AHA ID Card and Badge set unlocked, you can find them under the Customization tab in the lobby. If you’re having trouble finding them, here’s a full breakdown of where to look.

You have to navigate through quite a few different pages, tabs, and sections to successfully find the AHA Advocate ID Card and Badge, so they can be a bit tough to locate at first. Look for the bright red color of both items to make finding them a bit easier once you’re in the right section.

You can only grab the AHA Advocate ID Card and Badge until Nov. 15. After this date, it’ll no longer be obtainable and likely will never return, as has been the case with all other special event items. Because of this, you’ll want to be sure to log on and grab it while you can if you’re interested in permanently adding it to your collection.

If you’re looking for additional items you can unlock, there are lots of tasks you can work on to claim more freebies. Consider working on challenges like Artist’s Retreat, Entangled Terror, and Farmhouse Fieldwork next.

#3850. Venom-toothed Noxious Terminids are soon to infest Helldivers 2, and it's your noble job to sterilise the galaxy for Super Earth

Helldivers 2 isn't slowing down any time soon, and according to Edwin's recent interview with Arrowhead CCO Johan Pilestedt, it'll continue to be Arrowhead's main priority for the future. As if Helldivers 2 wasn't full of enough horrors for our brave Super Earth Helldivers to shoot at for the betterment of galactic democracy, its next update is due to add an entirely new Terminid subspecies, the Noxious Terminids.

First up on are the Noxious Scavengers. These horrible little (see: huge) things skitter around at high speed and are loaded with deadly poison, but are thankfully at least fragile. Liberal use of area-of-effect weapons such as flamethrowers, explosives and flamethrowers are recommended to avoid being overrun by these horse-sized insects. Then there's the Noxious Spewer, which is not only fast like its smaller brethren despite its larger size, but also equipped with a web projectile which locks a Helldiver in place, vulnerable to a fatal bite. Oh, and if you dare shoot its soft underbelly, it violently explodes, with the same web fluid covering a wide area around it. The poison inflicted by these creatures' bites is a new damage over time effect that can blur vision, slow movement, eat away at your health, and make you fear this may be the end for you — so it's a bit like getting the flu (get your jabs!)

HELLDIVERS™ 2 | A Cleaner Galaxy Starts With You Watch on YouTube

This update also makes the change that bug caves can be found across many more worlds across the galaxy, leading troopers down tunnels with limited visibility and claustrophobic dead ends. Super Earth's propaganda, sorry, I mean, guidance, describes the galactic sterilisation program quite simply: locate the invasive species, identify the horrific monsters at the barrel of your flamethrower, and sterilise (burn to cinders). The guidance also, hilariously, includes the line: "Super Earth reminds you that ammunition is cheaper than antivenom." Now, get out there and rid our beautiful democracy of this vile pestilence.

Here's how you unlock medicine upgrades in Phantom Blade Zero

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Phantom Blade Zero medicine upgrades aren't unlocked until about halfway through the game while you’re exploring Pangzhen. They're obviously incredibly useful, so you'll want to get access to this system as soon as you can to start enhancing the healing power and increases the number of uses of your many healing items. To help you do just that, I've explained everything you need to know about upgrading medicine in Phantom Blade Zero below.

To unlock medicine upgrades in Phantom Blade Zero, you just need to go inside the Green Serpent House in the Backstreets area of Pangzhen and speak to Xie Xiaorong at the counter. Conveniently, the medicine upgrade system is folded into the general 'Upgrade Equipment' menu that you can use at any Bell, so you don't have to keep visiting the Green Serpent House to boost your medicines.

Depending on how far through the game you are, reaching the Green Serpent House might take you a while, even if you're already in Pangzhen. But follow the main quests through the desolate town and you'll eventually reach the house.

Upgrading medicine costs a few thousand Remnant Dust and one Healer's Memory per level. Higher upgrade levels require more Remnant Dust and rarer Healer's Memories – for example, levels 1 and 2 require a single Apprentice Healer's Memory but levels 3 and 4 require a Skilled Healer's Memory, and so on. Healer's Memories of all qualities are found throughout the game and can be bought in limited quantities from the Bell shop.

Importantly, medicine upgrades are permanent and cannot be reverted in the same way weapon upgrades can be. My advice is therefore to focus your upgrades on only the medicine items you're currently using. That way you should have some spare Healer's Memories to perform some instant upgrades if you change your Medicine to something better.

Furthermore, while you're in Pangzhen, you'll eventually get the Phantom Blade Zero Flaming Mane weapon which will finally allow you get inside the other Serpent Houses around the world, which are critical to the main quest.

Before you head off to the Pangzhen Backstreets, you may want to wrap up the Phantom Blade Zero Four Fierce Axes quest first. Then you can go there and hunt down the Phantom Blade Zero Mandate Encampment Key and complete the Phantom Blade Zero Flesh Lily quest.

#3848. Modern Warfare 4 on Switch 2 has much worse input lag than PS5

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Switch 2 has noticeably worse input lag than on PS5, which could put Nintendo players at a disadvantage in multiplayer.

Digital Foundry's tech review measured multiplayer latency at 81ms when docked and an average of 100ms in portable mode, against 49ms on PS5. Testing used wireless controllers on both consoles (a Switch 2 Pro Controller and a DualSense), and portable results ranged from 83ms at best to 125ms at worst.

Digital Foundry said "responsiveness here simply isn't as good as on other consoles", and described the lag in portable mode as "actually deleterious to performance" (thanks, IGN).

Beyond the lag, Digital Foundry is fairly positive about the port. Multiplayer runs at 60fps most of the time, and if your TV supports VRR, you'll notice the drops less. The campaign is capped at 30fps and resolution is dynamic.

Docked with DLSS on, the game targets 900p, but Digital Foundry saw it drop to 450p in busier scenes, such as the Paris vehicle chase. In portable mode, the target is 720p, with drops to 360p.

It's been 13 years since a Call of Duty game last appeared on Nintendo hardware, with Ghosts on Wii U in 2013. The series' return is the result of a 10-year deal Microsoft offered Nintendo while it sought regulatory approval for its $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard.

Yesterday we reported that Activision has apologised to the bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it will remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Welcome to FOV 90, an FPS column from staff writer Morgan Park. Every other week, I cover topics relevant to first-person shooter enjoyers, spanning everything from multiplayer and singleplayer to the old and the new.

Welcome back to a special election day edition of FOV 90, the only FPS column that insists American readers vote twice today—first on important videogame matters right here, then on crucial *gestures at everything else* matters at your designated polling place.

Today we return from a totally planned hiatus, during which the PC Gamer community settled both the best RTS unit and best horror games, to dispute an issue of far greater significance: The greatest FPS mode of all time. Round 2's matchups reflected an enthusiasm for classic team-based formats with a respectable turnout as well for modern arrivals like Battle Royale. I asked you to make some tough calls and you showed up.

Over 2,500 votes were cast across Round 2 matchups, and the results are in.

A decisive victory in each contest. Every mode I voted for came out on top, which I honestly didn't expect. Sure, TDM over Battle Royale makes sense, but an 82% majority tells me that the most popular shooter format of today has not usurped the classics among PC Gamer readers (same). But even so, this is where I expected Conquest (a chaotic fight over territory) to accept a humble defeat to Bomb Defusal (the gold standard of competitive PvP). I'm glad I was wrong!

Not as much comment sparring went down this time, but I would like to highlight one reader comment that got me thinking:

And here's how PC Gamer's staff reacted to the results:

"What's notable to me about the final four is that they mostly don't put individuals on the spot. In Infection, Battle Royale, and Bomb Defusal, you can wind up being the last survivor, with all the pressure on you to bring it home. That's not really the case in TDM, Conquest, Payload, or CTF, which usually allow unlimited respawns (or in the case of Conquest, end when respawns run out). CTF does require individual flag runner heroism, but as part of a team effort."

"The continued dominance of Payload is vexing to me: I've always thought it was Fine, but an all-conquering hero? Maybe I'm just sore it bodied Gun Game in the first round—I was a fan back when it was a modded Counter-Strike mode first and foremost. If Payload beats out the all time classic, Capture the Flag, this round, we may have to reexamine this whole "democracy" thing."

"CTF had its time, and was at its peak in the various iterations of Tribes, a context in which you could literally swoop in to snatch the banner. But I don't think it stands up if we're evaluating these as modern modes. Otherwise, it's tough to see Bomb Defusal fizzle—Counter-Strike's competitive mode holds up wonderfully as the premier FPS esport, which says a lot given that it's asymmetrical."

But alas, it's time to bury our dead and move on. Round 3 is on!

Read up on the matchups below and vote for your favorite. Round 3 voting closes on Sunday, November 8 at 11:59 PM PDT. The more votes we get, the more interesting the results, so tell your friends! Next week we'll be back to share the results and begin the FINALS.

AKA: Team Slayer (Halo) // Warfare (Hell Let Loose)

Intimate team-based action, or large-scale territory control?

AKA: It's always Payload and CTF, because they're perfect names

Two modes about escorting an object where the other team doesn't want it to go, but only one moves on.

#3844. At Dead of Night sequel The Great Hugo is coming "(very) soon"

Baggy Cat Games, the team behind viral FMV horror game At Dead Of Night, has confirmed that a sequel is "coming (very) soon".

At Dead Of Night 2: The Great Hugo picks up where the original game left off and reunites us with Maya as she heads off to investigate a large Tudor manor house.

At Dead Of Night became famous quickly during the pandemic thanks to streamers and content creators like Markiplier, 8-BitRyan, John Wolfe, and DomPlays, who introduced us to Jimmy Hall, a creepy hotel landlord hellbent on recruiting an audience for his late-night comedy show and psychopathic comedy alter ego, Hugo Punch.

The new game, subtitled The Great Hugo, picks up half a decade later.

"Five years later, Maya is still haunted by her experiences in Sea View Hotel," the blurb teases. "Desperate for answers she remembers the ghost box she used in the hotel, left there when she escaped.

"After searching on [auction] sites and in antique shops, she finds a similar looking device, but can’t get it to work. She contacts an old friend and counsellor, Quinn, who had helped her understand her supernatural experiences in the hotel. Quinn recognises the device and knows where they were made - by an inventor who used to live in a large Tudor manor house not far from Sea View - but warns her against trying to get it working. However, Maya ignores his advice and goes on her own investigation."

Quite how long "(very) soon" is, we don't yet know, but we'll keep you posted.

Game sales are up by 18.8% compared to this time last year

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Nintendo has confirmed that the Switch 2 has sold 26.35 million consoles, down 37.4% from last year.

In its latest financial results – which cover the period between July and September 2026 – Nintendo confirms that a further 6.49 Nintendo Switch 2 consoles were sold in the quarter; this puts the total number of consoles sold to 26.35 million since it launched last June. However, compared to the same period last year, Switch 2 sales are down 37.4%, with Switch 2 selling 10.36 million units during the quarter in 2025. The Switch 2 had a very strong first year, becoming the fastest-selling console of all time, thanks in part to people actually being able to buy the console, proving Nintendo's rumored decision to delay it for that reason to be the right one.

For comparison, the original Nintendo Switch had sold 19.67 million consoles by the end of its 15th month. Sony reported in its second year that PS5 consoles had sold 19.3 million units by the end of March 2022 (16 months after launch). So while the Switch 2 is losing compared to the Switch 2, it's doing better than its contemporaries. And while Xbox doesn't reveal console sales figures, reports indicate the Xbox Series X|S had shipped around 28.3 million units by June 2024, so it's safe to say the Switch 2 is probably outperforming it, too.

Despite a fall in console sales, Nintendo says Switch 2 game sales were up 18.8% compared to this time last year. Naturally this would be the case given more people have Switch 2 consoles and there are more games, with the console only really having Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza around launch (there's also Welcome Tour and Drag x Drive, I guess). Splatoon Raiders and Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave got off to great starts, selling 2.42 million and 1.34 million copies respectively. And perhaps most importantly, Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 2.89 million copies, which means for the time being it's done better than Marvel's Wolverine; nature is healing.

Check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review to see why it's the highest-rated game of 2026. You can also read our Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock live blog if you're keen to grab one of Nintendo's fancy new consoles for the game's launch.

#3842. Phantom Blade Zero is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, selling over 4 million copies in three days

Phantom Blade Zero studio S-Game has announced that its debut title has sold more than 4m copies in its first 72 hours on sale. The game's official X account broke the news alongside a celebratory message, though without providing a per-platform breakdown of copies sold.

"Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support!" the developer wrote on X.

Phantom Blade Zero is available on Steam and PlayStation 5, but the 4m figure also includes sales made on the China-exclusive Tencent WeGame PC launcher. Prior to launch, Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott estimated Phantom Blade Zero to have sold over 1m copies before it had even released.

It was always clear the third-person character action game was going to be a hit, we just had to wait for actual figures to be released.

Phantom Blade Zero attracted over 431,000 concurrent players on Steam at launch, a figure that kept risking and rising into the weekend, ultimately settling at a massive 833,921 peak concurrent (via SteamDB). Just in case it wasn't already clear, this is Steam's biggest launch of the year so far, beating the likes of Forza Horizon 6 and far outpacing all other major releases such as Onimusha: Way of the Sword, The Blood of Dawnwalker, and Ace Combat 8.

Despite the very strong opening weekend's numbers, Phantom Blade Zero has not been able to match or exceed the performance of Black Myth: Wukong, 2024's also-Chinese developed triple-A action game, just yet. The breakout hit, estimated to have sold 30m copies since, is one of Steam's largest debuts ever, peaking at 2,415,714 concurrent players at launch.

In Eurogamer's Phantom Blade Zero review, Emma Kent spoke highly of much of the game, but was critical of its underwhelming narrative and lack of consistency, writing: "This game is exceptional in so many areas - the animations, the beautiful environments - and when the combat works, the sense of flow is incredible. Then you walk into a boss battle and feel all that power fade, like you're waiting your turn to get hits in with a wooden sword."

#3841. Play as water and rain on wildfires in Atuel, a short, free game about the power and vulnerability of nature

Well, have you played Atuel? If not, you can do so within the next hour - it's a tiny, free, 25-minute walking sim, albeit one with little actual walking on account of you playing most of it as a river. More of a running sim, really.

Have You Played? is an endless stream of game retrospectives.

Technically, Atuel calls itself a "documentary game", and not without justification. While its sweeping Patagonian landscapes are rendered with a dreamy otherworldliness, and certain moments are downright mystic, the whole watery journey is based directly on the Atuel River that runs through western Argentina. As you drift downhill, taking control of water, clouds, and the local wildlife, you'll hear real-life scientists and historians monologuing on the Atuel and its relationship with the human cultures it's nourished. Mercifully, these are delivered with thoughtfulness as well as earnestness, maintaining the game's contemplative atmosphere without making it sound like the audio guide to a museum of Birmingham canals.

A few bends in, Atuel also takes on the climate crisis, directing you away from the soothing freshwater and into wildfires and parched riverbeds. I'd say this was preaching to the choir, at least for anyone who a) desires a functioning planet and b) learned about the water cycle in primary school, but then it isn't really preaching. Rather, developers Matajuegos weave between the beauty of the Earth and the need to protect it quite gracefully, and end their river tour on a more hopeful note than its darker moments may have intimated.

There's plenty else to leave an outsized impression in your memory matter: the understated, naturally-textured soundtrack, for instance, or the patiently gradual zoom-outs that slowly unveil the Andes' wild splendour. For me, and without wanting to undermine the importance or the accuracy of Atuel's environmental point, it was mainly just nice – therapeutic, even – to float through its gorgeous, surreal scenery like a cloud. And sometimes, as one. You can download it for free from Steam and Itch, with a pay-what-you-want option on the latter.

Countless sickos of a certain vintage just breathed sighs of relief.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It's been a good few months for Remedy Entertainment. In its latest financial results, the Finnish game developer announced that its third quarter revenue had more than tripled to €39.6 million ($44.3 million) from the €12.2 million ($13.7 million) it made during the same quarter last year.

That spike in income is all thanks to preorders and launch sales of Control Resonant—of which only the first seven days of sales were counted in Remedy's third quarter figures. On October 15, Resonant sold its millionth copy, making it the fastest-selling game in Remedy history.

"This is our first self-published game of this scale, built on our own Control IP," said Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, who was appointed to the position earlier this year. "Praised by players and critics alike, it marks a defining milestone for the company."

Gaudechon also noted that "close to 50%" of Resonant players were Control newcomers, indicating the sequel had achieved "a key goal" of expanding the audience for Remedy's brand of stylish interdimensional sicko content. Its mission for the immediate future, the CEO said, is to continue delivering Resonant to more interested players—2.4 million of whom still have yet to turn their wishlists into purchases, according to Remedy data.

"Our priority now is to get Control Resonant into the hands of more players. Excellent player reviews, penetration in all our target markets and a substantial outstanding wishlist base give a solid foundation for the game's longer-term sales potential, supported by both organic visibility as well as our targeted marketing activities," Gaudechon said. "As with the launch, we will invest with discipline, prioritizing actions with a clear return."

While Remedy's operating profit margin was still thin for the quarter—1.5% of revenue, or €0.6 million—Resonant's strong launch performance is a welcome change of pace from where the studio was at the end of last year. In November 2025, it had posted an operating loss of €16.4 million thanks to the flop of FBC Firebreak. From the sounds of it, Remedy's aiming to continue that momentum with whatever work it has planned next.

"Alongside the launch of Control Resonant, our other projects are proceeding in the pipeline," Gaudechon said. "Sales over the remainder of the year will ultimately define our financial year 2026. Control Resonant gives us a solid foundation for growth."

#3838. Soulframe to launch into free open beta this week, as Warframe devs go head-to-head with WoW: Forever

Soulframe's Preludes (its own version of a beta) is finally opening its doors to the whole world ahead of the Verse of the Veilands update. Starting this week, anyone who wants to can simply download the game and hop in, no invite required.

The date this happens is an interesting one: 6th November. That's two days after the release of World of Warcraft: Forever and the same week as Old School RuneScape's Hardcore worlds, so it's suddenly become a pretty packed month for MMO enthusiasts.

This comes after three years of closed testing for the fantasy action MMORPG, which players have been able to gradually see firsthand through sporadic invites. With Soulframe suffering delays since its first reveal, brief invite events have already occurred over this period. Even locked away, the game has received multiple substantial updates over the years, including new quests, Pacts (classes), factions and so on.

As for what newcomers to Soulframe can look forward to when Soulframe opens its doors, the Verse of the Veillands update is bringing a total overhaul of the map progression system this month. After the completion of an early quest, players are introduced to a corrupted landscape, the Veillands, which they must purify.

As you do so, new resources will be obtainable and side activities like fishing will be unlocked. You'll also be able to train up a small wolf pet into a full-on mount in the process. Previously, players were just thrust into the open world to explore and figure things out as they go, so this should provide something of an introduction to the game's open map. It won't be totally finished when released mind you, with updates to the Veillands system coming in the future.

On top of that, there's a new Pact called the Ode Shrike coming with the update. It's a tricksy trapper with spikes, balloon snares, bombs and chains to disrupt enemies as you whittle them down.

Could this be enough to win people over to Digital Extreme's newest project? Time will tell - but in the meantime its long-lasting sci-fi MMO Warframe is taking players to the Tau system in a major next step in the game's narrative this December. It comes with a detective noir inspired main quest, playable warframe, and even an in-universe Poker equivalent.

#3837. Silica, an FPS and RTS hybrid that mixes a smidge of Dune and Helldivers together, has left early access and entered 1.0

The concept of fusing an RTS and an FPS always sounds like a fun one, and since 2023 Martin Melichárek has been trying to make a new take on the combination under the watchful eye of DayZ devs Bohemia Interactive through Silica. Today marks the day that Silica leaves early access and enters 1.0, fully fleshing out its hybrid and mish mash of Dune's Arrakis and Helldivers' Terminids.

Digging into Silica a touch more deeply, it is a sci-fi shooter set on a planet where there's a fancy resource you're trying to mine that definitely isn't the spice. There are two warring factions competing for said resource, when, uh oh! Some bug-ish, giant aliens aren't very happy you're doing all that. So, you can either join the fray on the ground with some classic first-person shooting alongside your friends, or you can take the role of commander and dictate your artillery from above.

The 1.0 update obviously comes with a few additions, namely the Centauri Campaign, a "story-driven single-player experience set in the war for Baltarus. It opens with a cinematic intro and features fully voiced mission briefings and in-game dialogue. Between missions, a 3D planetary globe tracks the war as territory changes hands." Commanding your army should be a better experience now too, with the ability to "arrange units into formations, issue more precise movement and attack orders, and quickly select all units of the same type. Improved AI targeting and vehicle movement also help your armies operate more effectively in large-scale battles."

Beyond that, 1v1 matchmaking has been added in, where you can fight against another commander. The Steam Workshop sandbox tools have been expanded for building your own scenarios and sharing them with others. And there are a whole bunch of bug fixes, quality-of-life improvements and additions, and more. You can read about some of those in more detail in this handy little blog post. If you like what Silica is putting down, then you can pick it up on Steam.

Fans are already worried about what they are going to miss in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping if they choose to see it on a regular screen rather than in IMAX.

Over on Twitter, IMAX Downtown Indiana teased the expanded aspect ratio, showing fans what to expect if they see the prequel movie on the biggest screen possible. However, it looks like most of the wider scenes take place in the arena, meaning fans who don't have access to an IMAX cinema will miss out on some of the action.

More picture. More of Panem. 🔥 Filmed for IMAX, #TheHungerGames: #SunriseontheReaping features expanded imagery that lets you see more of the action on the giant screen. https://t.co/A6YfvFzHKxNovember 4, 2026

"Our place doesn’t have IMAX," said one disappointed fan, and another added, "The difference between a regular screen and IMAX is totally insane." However, one eagle-eyed fan spotted that a key death takes place in the background, right under the IMAX boundary. We don't want to spoil the story for those who haven't read the book, so we won't reveal whose death is shown, but it might mean that regular cinema-goers will miss out on this.

Sunrise on the Reaping is the first film in the franchise to have been filmed for IMAX. According to IMAX, it features over 45 minutes of footage filmed in 1.90:1 expanded aspect ratio. It is thought that the ratio will change as the tributes rise up into the arena, just as the screen widened slightly in the 2013 sequel The Hunger Games: Catching Fire.

IMAX is causing quite the stir in the movie industry, with many projects having a number of scenes filmed for the wider screens. Earlier this year, Christopher Nolan made history by releasing the first movie completely filmed for IMAX, The Odyssey. Screenings at IMAX 70mm cinemas were sold out for months, with many movie buffs flying into cities with IMAX cinemas just so they could see the ancient Greek epic as Nolan intended.

Set 24 years before the first film, Sunrise on the Reaping follows 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) as he is drafted into the 50th Hunger Games, where the game makers send in twice as many players as usual to mark the second Quarter Quell. We first met Haymitch, played by Woody Harrelson, as Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark's mentor in the original saga. Excitingly, the new movie features a cameo from Katniss and Peeta stars Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping hits theaters on November 20. In the meantime, check out our guide to all the other most exciting upcoming movies of the year, or the major movie release dates still to come.

#3835. All Cloudreach Falls Aniimo locations

The Whisperwake Isles region has opened up in Aniimo, and by exploring this vast land, you can find and collect all kinds of new creatures. One of the areas you must traverse is Cloudreach Falls, which has quite a collection of Aniimo for you to find.

In each unique area you can explore, tracking down all of the Aniimo who call the region home can be tough, as they’ve all got only a few specific spawn locations, and many of them can only be found under special conditions. If you’re struggling to find any of these creatures, here are the locations of all Aniimo found around the Cloudfall Reach region in Aniimo.

In total, there are 14 unique Aniimo you can encounter around Cloudreach Falls. Some of them are exclusive to this region, while others can be found around a few different areas in Aniimo.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Each of the 14 Aniimo wandering around Cloudreach Falls has a few different habitat locations. Here’s exactly where to find all Cloudreach Falls Aniimo and a breakdown of any special conditions that must be met to get them.

Jeglid spawns at quite a few spots around Cloudreach Falls, including the upper middle region and the lower middle area, close to the teleport points in both areas. You can also find them around the lower eastern edge of this region.

You can find Jeglid (Tempest form) near the middle, upper right edge of Cloudreach Falls. This Aniimo only spawns during stormy weather, so you’ll have to wait and watch for this condition, or work to change the weather for it to spawn. It only spawns around the two spots marked below, making it fairly easy to spot once the conditions are right.

You can find Jeburst close to the water near the middle of Cloudreach Falls, east of the teleport point in this area. Jeburst also spawns a bit further south, near some water in this region.

Jeburst (Tempest form) can be found in the water pool at the bottom of the waterfall near the northeast end of this area. This Aniimo only spawns in stormy weather, though, so you must wait for these conditions to find and catch one.

Dewlop (Waterfall form) is pretty prevalent, with lots of different spawn regions around this area. This Aniimo is so common that you’re likely to run into it naturally while simply exploring. If not, though, you can visit any of the areas marked below to encounter them. They’re particularly abundant up north.

The Dewple (Waterfall form) is a bit of a special one, as it can only be found at one specific spot in the Cloudreach Falls area. To locate it, head to the spot marked below, find the large rock in the pool of water at this location, and use an Aniimo ability to destroy the rock. Jump into the water geyser that’s released upon breaking the rock, and capture the Dewple (Waterfall form) Aniimo once it appears in this stream.

You can find Saws swimming around a few different areas, including near the middle teleport point, close to the south end of the area, and on the small island a bit offshore. This Aniimo sticks to the water, so when searching for them, be sure to look in the water to find this species.

Whirlbite spawns around most of the same areas as Saws, and they also stick close to the water. You can go searching for them in the water pools up north, near the south end of Cloudreach Falls, and over on the small island off the coast.

To get Whirlbite (Prismana form), head to the Bloom marked on the map below. Nurture this Bloom frequently and catch all Aniimo that spawn around it. Eventually, you’ll increase the Prismana Flow state enough for Whirlbite (Prismana form) to spawn. When they do, you’ll get a special pop-up letting you know, and their location will be marked on the map.

You can find Eko in abundance around the northern end of Cloudreach Falls. Look all around the teleport point situated in the middle of this area to spot lots of them wandering around.

There are only two habitat spawn spots for Eklue. One is southwest of the middle teleport point and the other is northeast of it, close to the edge of the island. This Aniimo is fairly rare, so scan carefully to ensure you don’t miss it.

Ekrim can be found at three locations around Cloudreach Falls. One is located a bit east of the middle teleport point, and the other two are slightly south of it. This Aniimo is also quite rare, so there’s only one to be found at each spot.

You can find loads of Puffby roaming around the tall cliffs situated near the northwest end of Cloudreach Falls. They’re fairly common as long as you’re hunting for them in this area.

Hypnowls are by far the most abundant Aniimo in the Cloudreach Falls region. Of all the creatures you can find here, this is the one you’re likely going to run into the most, especially when exploring the lower southern part of this area.

If you’re looking for more to get done in Aniimo, consider working on some other tasks next, like finding Umbral Aniimo, checking out all Astra shops, vendors, games, and what they sell, and getting Sparkling Cubes.
