FBI may be in its ninth season on the 2026 TV schedule, but the series continues to keep fans on the edge of their seats. Following OA’s undercover storyline, one would think that things are back to normal at 26 Fed. Unfortunately, there may be another shakeup coming. After the end of this week’s episode, I’m worried that another major exit is near.

Throughout the Dick Wolf CBS procedural’s run, there have been a handful of exits. In the last couple of years, FBI has seen three big departures. It seemed like the curse could be done after Juliana Aidén Martinez’s addition at the beginning of Season 8, but alas, another could be coming.

In this week’s episode, “Atonement,” Scola (John Boyd) told the team that Nina (Shantel VanSanten) was offered to run her own task force. It was great news, but Scola didn’t seem too sure about it. He later tells Eva (Aidén Martinez) that the job is in San Diego. While at first he told Nina not to take it, he eventually calls her to say that she should after his conversation with Eva.

Scola was scared about uprooting their life and moving across the country, which is why he told Nina not to take it in the first place. His hesitation is understandable. He’s lived in New York his entire life, their son, Dougie, is getting older, and he has his job. That being said, Nina’s worked hard to get to where she is, and it’s a great promotion for her, which is why Scola came to his senses and told her she should take it. They’ll figure it out.

Whether Boyd is actually leaving FBI remains unknown. VanSanten is set to return to the series on Monday, November 16, but little has been shared about the episode beyond the fact that the team will work alongside Nina to intercept a criminal on the Most Wanted list. Scola and Nina have gone through a lot over the last several seasons, between breakups, makeups, near-deaths, and welcoming their son. While I would absolutely hate to say goodbye to Scola, it would only make sense for him to follow Nina to San Diego so they can stay together and raise their son in the same proximity and not 2,800 miles apart.

Nothing is confirmed, and it’s not even clear if Nina will end up taking the job. It’s likely we’ll get more information during VanSanten’s return on November 16, but fans may have to brace themselves. Boyd has been on FBI since Season 2. It’s hard to imagine the show without him, but at this point, unfortunately, anything is possible. For now, we’ll just have to wait and see. New episodes of FBI air on Mondays at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

#3743. Xbox Accused Of ‘Sabotaging’ Arkane: ‘We Want To Finish Blade And Release It To The Players’

Xbox is running out of time to find a buyer for Arkane as a December deadline approaches, and a French union is now blaming Microsoft’s gaming division for allegedly “sabotaging” the Dishonored and Deathloop maker as it attempts to finish its latest project, Marvel’s Blade.

“Today, as work on Blade is going fine, and that the level of quality of the game to be expected is on part (sic) with what Arkane has accustomed its players, workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded,” the French game union Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu VidÃ©o (STJV) wrote in an open letter on November 4.

Marvel’s Blade was revealed back in 2022 and is rumored to still be a couple of years away from release. STJV has accused Xbox of slowing progress by instituting a 19-month hiring freeze that “artificially caused delay and additional cost.” The union also argues that closing Arkane at this point would “probably be more expensive than finishing the game.”

It claims there are currently 217 people at Arkane who would be impacted by a studio closure. Microsoft extended its search for a buyer for the storied 25-year-old immersive sim maker and has reportedly received bids from Ubisoft and others. It also looked at trying to do a management buyout, as has happened with Compulsion Games and Undead Labs.

“We want our studio to live on and produce games, we want to finish Blade and release it to the players, as well as the many games the future holds for Arkane,” STJV wrote. In the event that no sale is possible, the union has called on Microsoft to make redundancy payments of roughly $225,000 per employee, as well as provide other post-employment benefits.

“The decision to close Arkane is solely the brutal application of a never-ending search for maximum profit optimization,” STJV argued. “Arkane is profitable. Just not profitable enough for Microsoft.”

#3742. Despite hardware worries and rising costs, Sony says PlayStation 6 development is on track and "progressing as scheduled"

Today, Thursday 5th November, 2026, Sony shared its latest financial results, reporting on the second quarter of financial year 2026 for the company. In a wide-ranging set of statements, we learned that the company's overall profits have been charged by the box office success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and that its annual profit outlook has been raised following a particularly successful quarter.

As for PlayStation, Sony CFO Lin Tao hinted at the status of the PlayStation 6 - not yet named as such - which is currently being worked on in the company's gaming division. She noted that the console is "progressing as scheduled" and that staff are making "solid progress" on the machine (thanks, VGC). Tao also revealed that it's been a strong year for the PS5; total sales for the console have reached 97.9 million, thanks to a further 2.6 million sales throughout July, August and September 2026.

The most interesting bytes of information teased out of this call relate to Tao's claim that Sony has been able to offset the rise in memory costs via cost reductions and price increases, all helped by a yearly operating income boost of 89 percent. Sony notes that it has secured enough memory hardware for its next business year, which helps prepare the ground for PlayStation 6 production which should kick off in earnest next year.

"Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform."

Tao outlines that Sony is beginning to pivot towards this new platform in terms of both investment and production, and that Sony will "attach great importance to a new platform and make the necessary investments for that." This platform - the as-yet-unofficially-named PS6 - will be announced "at an appropriate time in the future".

This all follows reports that the PS6's memory and storage alone reportedly cost more than $680, and that there is still no hard release date set for the console. In light of the fact that console manufacturing is being heavily impacted by the on-going component shortage, many are expecting the price of the base PS6 to be over $1000. We will have to see what Sony announces over the next year before we know for certain.

#3741. Jackson Olson Jokes About Impressing GF Maggie's Dad Pat Sajak on Vacation

Savannah Bananas star Jackson Olson is winning over the entire Sajak family — one TikTok at a time.

“First trip with the Sajak fam = success … I think?” Olson, 29, wrote via TikTok on Tuesday, November 3, alongside footage with girlfriend Maggie Sajak and her famous dad, former Wheel of Fortune host Pat Sajak, lip-syncing a beloved Gilmore Girls scene.

“What do you have to offer?” Pat, 80, mouthed before Olson replied, “Nothing, only this,” and started dancing. (Sean Gunn’s Kirk Gleason originally said the now-viral “nothing” line in his character’s avant-garde short film, which premiered during a town movie night during season 2.)

After receiving a look from Pat, the Dancing With the Stars season 35 castoff buried his face in his hands and walked off camera.

Olson has been dating Maggie, 31, since April.

“It’s really cool because we’re obviously living very different lives right now on the opposite side of the country, but we’re able to come together and just have an awesome relationship,” Olson exclusively told Us in May. “I feel like in any relationship, you’re trying to figure out how to see each other as frequently as possible, which is never something that I thought in my past I was going to want to do … but now I really do.”

He continued at the time, “It’s just about planning and making sure you’re setting aside time to see each other and make really cool experiences happen because a start of a relationship never happens again. You only get one chance at a start of a relationship.”

While speaking with Us, Olson revealed that he already met Pat.

“He’s a great guy,” he gushed. “Everybody’s nervous to meet the father of the person they’re dating, or mother or both. I’m a very weird person, I’m a very out there person. I’m not going to hold back who I am as a person, and people seem to enjoy that company. I’m happy that I’m able to be myself truly in every aspect now.”

Olson also had Maggie’s support during his DWTS tenure.

“It’s so awesome [to have her here]. I try not to look at her during the dance because I know that she’s smiling,” he told Us in September, weeks before his Halloween Horror Nights elimination. “I know that she’s so excited and smiling. And if I looked at her, I would just like be like, ‘Ah!’ But it’s awesome, and she’s so supportive of both of us, too. She was wearing the Team Banana ballroom shirt today, so that was cool.”

Neither Critical Role diehards nor Hololive vtuber fans could've predicted that they'd work together to film a new tabletop roleplaying series. Shattered Legends is the product of a collaboration that might sound bizarre at first but makes perfect sense when you consider vtubers are basically just voice actors, like just about everyone else in Critical Role's orbit.

Matt Mercer certainly sees them that way. He tells PC Gamer that filming Shattered Legends with Hololive vtubers gave him a "deeper understanding and appreciation for the skill and talent that each of these performers has." The only challenge, he says, was the technical logistics of filming a show with a mix of humans and 2D anime girls.

The original idea for Shattered Legends, before it even had a name, was a pitch from Nerissa Ravencroft, Hololive's "Demon of Sound" vtuber. A long-time fan of Critical Role, Ravencroft says she could barely believe it when her manager told her they were up for it: "I was in awe for multiple days."

"Growing up, I never had friends or knew anybody who ran a TTRPG campaign, so it’s been a heavy desire to play one for a long time," she says. "I just so happen to be one of the luckiest girls in the world, as I get to play with not only my fellow [Hololive vtubers], but Critical Role!"

Ravencroft took the lead on Hololive's side, creating her own character, working with artists on the visuals and unique vtuber models based on everyone's characters, and helping produce an original song.

The story of Shattered Legends was inspired by Berserk and Soulsborne games. All the vtubers—which includes Ravencroft, Mori Calliope, Gigi Murin, and Shiori Novella—wanted to tell a darker story than fans might've expected. Mercer and Marisha Ray, who played alongside the vtubers, helped them fit it into Critical Role's existing setting Exandria as a self-contained "canon-ish" campaign.

The group will be playing Daggerheart, Critical Role's own fantasy TTRPG. For those unfamiliar with it, Daggerheart eschews D&D's d20 rolling system for two 12-sided dice, one representing your 'hope' and the other your 'fear'. If your hope roll is higher, you can spend a point of it to do something beneficial, but if fear is higher, the GM can use it whenever they want to challenge the players.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Mercer prefers Daggerheart when playing with new players and likes how the narrative dynamics "allow for baked-in tension and release, while also inviting players to collaborate in extremely creative ways."

Ravencroft, who is one of those new players, says she was "a bit intimidated" as someone who normally plays videogames, but found it easy once things got going, especially with Mercer and Ray at the table. "Having Matt as a GM for my first Daggerheart campaign is already crazy enough," she says, "but with an incredibly experienced and talented roleplayer and actress like Marisha, we were truly in the best hands possible."

Although the story fits neatly into six episodes, Mercer says there's "much promise of a wider world for these characters," and that "there's always room to pick up these seeds for future adventures" if people want it.

Shattered Legends will premiere on Ravencroft's YouTube channel in mid-November.

#3739. World of Warcraft: Forever is off to a great start with Blizzard's smoothest launch in memory

World of Warcraft: Forever came out last night. Those who stayed up were prepared for the usual from major WoW releases: long queues, disconnects, and server lag. However, save for a few minor hiccups here and there, things went off without a hitch.

Eurogamer can report first-hand that for European players who stayed up from, let's say 11pm - 3:50am last night, the login queues were short and constantly moving. Those who were very keen to get in the moment servers went live ran into unclickable server selection boxes, but backing out and re-joining the short queue fixed this problem swiftly.

Once you got in, there was very little server lag save for a lost spell cast or two, nor were constant random disconnects that would boot you out into the cold (I didn't get disconnected once - a record). As far as WoW launches go, an incredibly smooth first day.

This was acknowledged by World of Warcraft developers, such as executive producer Holly Longdale who wrote on X: "At the risk of jinxing things, so far so goodish which is crazy by itself. The team prepared a lot since the wildness of Beta. And this launch was crazier than the insanity we imagined but thankfully the team built plans and contingencies. They are incredible in my opinion.".

Josh "Aggrend" Greenfield, a senior game designer on World of Warcraft Forever, addressed some minor issues that did pop up. These include a zone population problem: in basic terms the megaservers split players into different shards, and some of these felt a bit empty of players. There was also a quirk with the various big boats and zeppelins dotted around the map, which were busted. Temporary portals were added to provide a workaround.

"Thanks for everyone making this a great, super smooth launch," Greenfield wrote. "I’m going to head home and 'go to sleep' now. Yep, sleeping. Totally not playing WoW Forever until 3am. Nope."

The reaction to this silky smooth launch has some players flabbergasted. "I can't believe how smooth this launch is" is the title of Reddit user Arizhela's post, currently topping the WoW Forever board. They continue: "I fully expected to not be able to play today, but I logged in with no queue and no lag."

Another post, created in the early hours of this morning, is dubbed: "Never take a day off for launch, they said" in which a WoW player regrets not booking some time off from work this week, expecting problems. "You've been finessed son," replied user SnooWalruses3948, while SirePuns shared in the shock: "The advice was sound, but this time around the developers hired a witch I tell you. The code must’ve been witchcraft, the hardware must’ve been blessed by a witch as well."

It is unclear just how well World of Warcraft: Forever's launch was, given the unsocialable and employment-averse release time in the dead of night for us Europeans, but it follows a record-breaking beta period in which many hopped back into the MMO. Impressions from this beta were largely positive, the magic of the old MMO seemingly recaptured.

Mckenna Grace has been working since she was a little kid, and at 20 years old, it feels like she’s done a bit of everything. She’s done drama, action, horror, romance and more, and in her next project, the book-to-screen adaptation of Sunrise on the Reaping, she’ll play out a deeply intense tragedy that also features massive action. However, while it’s clear she’s open to many kinds of projects and work, there is one thing she says no to: nudity. Surprisingly, her reasoning has to do with Disney.

As I said, when it comes to Grace's career, she's explored lots of different genres, which have put her in many different situations. I mean, in the last year alone, she’s worked on Regretting You, Five Nights at Freddy’s 2, Scream 7, PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie, The Last Kiss, Nimrods and Sunrise on the Reaping. Those are all very different movies, and during an interview with Cosmopolitan, she was asked if there are any kinds of roles she’d say no to. Here’s how she responded, and how nudity and Disney came into the conversation:

At this point, I definitely don’t do nudity or very hypersexual things. I respect anybody who can, but it’s terrifying to me. I don’t know if that’ll ever change. It’s not like I only do wholesome things—my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in Scream—but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday.

See, it’s obvious from her explanation that she has nothing against intimacy or nudity. And it seems like she has a lot of respect for actors who do work on projects that require it or very sexual sequences, like Off Campus, for example. However, it’s not her cup of tea, and I do see why.

As she said, she wants to be a Disney princess someday. If you’ve seen the best Disney movies, you know there’s a certain level of wholesomeness involved. That’s not to say an actor who participates in a project that involves sex scenes or nudity wouldn’t get a role as a Disney princess or prince. However, it’s clear Grace is trying to create an image for herself that makes her an unquestionable fit for one of these very wholesome roles.

I think she’s doing a good job at that too. I mean, before Teagan Croft and Milo Manheim were cast as Rapunzel and Flynn Rider for the live-action Tangled, Mckenna Grace and Mason Thames were popular fan casts for the parts. She legitimately looks like a princess, and her bubbly and bright personality fits right in with that kind of character too.

Now, getting back to what she said, she made it clear she’s not only going to do wholesome roles, and her work on the 2026 movie schedule clearly showcases that. I mean, Scream 7 is a horror movie, and as she said, she gets brutally murdered in it. Also, Sunrise on the Reaping is not for the faint of heart. As a fan of the book, I know how brutal the story is, and I know we’ll see Grace acting out some truly violent and intense moments.

However, while she’s willing to do work like that, she does have boundaries she does not want to cross. That means she’ll say no to projects that are hypersexual or involve nudity, which is totally respectable.

With that said, hopefully someday she’ll get her wish of being a Disney princess. While we wait for that to happen (because I do feel like it’s inevitable), you can catch Mckenna Grace in Sunrise on the Reaping on November 20.

#3736. GTA 6 Has Already Sold Nearly 8 Million Copies, One Data Firm Claims

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6PS5Rockstar GamesSalesXbox Series X/S

We are two weeks out from the start of Grand Theft Auto 6‘s global launch, and one data firm is claiming it’s already sold nearly 8 million copies. Not surprisingly, it also claims roughly three quarters of those sales are on PlayStation 5.

Data firm Sensor Tower has updated its GTA 6 sales tracker and currently has Rockstar Games’ latest open-world crime simulator at an estimated 7.71 million copies sold via pre-orders alone. That comes out to an estimated $751 million in revenue, with Sensor Tower claiming a breakdown of roughly 74 percent of copies sold on PS5 compared to 26 percent on Xbox Series X/S.

The trendline shows an uptick in the rate of pre-orders sold following the extended gameplay reveal on Netflix, and it sure seems like Sony’s exclusive marketing campaign for GTA 6 has helped give it a bump over Xbox. The fact that a base PS5 is cheaper than a base Xbox Series X could also be a factor. According to Sensor Tower, 1.97 million copies have been pre-ordered on Xbox compared to 5.74 million on PS5.

Given Xbox’s struggles this console generation, that number isn’t great, but it could be much worse. Especially when it has to resort to sticking hardware inside of an alligator to get around marketing prohibitions on talking about GTA 6 coming to Xbox Series X/S.

To put the overall estimate of 7.71 million pre-order sales in perspective, Cyberpunk 2077 reportedly amassed around 8 million total pre-orders in the run up to its 2020 launch. That number also already puts it just behind Resident Evil Requiem‘s estimated 8.5 million sales which, for now at least, are enough to make Capcom’s horror sequel the second best-selling game of 2026 in the U.S. so far.

And it’s just a small chunk of what some analysts are predicting for total launch window sales. Financial services firm Piper Sandler is predicting 45 million sales when GTA 6 comes out. Anything less might be seen as disappointing, even if it would still be well over the $800 million GTA 5 made during its first 24 hours. It’s going to be the biggest game launch ever. We’ll see if it ends up being big enough for Take-Two’s investors.

#3735. PlayStation sees record high player numbers and increased revenue for Q2 2026, and a lot of that success is down to Marvel's Wolverine

As part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the company, and sets a new record high.

In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year.

Notably, despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed. The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei, meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025.

More people playing consoles, and for longer - it must all be good news for Sony right? Well, not all the graphs are showing growth. PS5 hardware sales continue to gradually decline: in the reporting period, Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles, down from 4 million in the same quarter in 2025. But, with 100 million PS5 units out in the wild, and 127 million PlayStation accounts across the whole ecosystem, Sony doesn't seem that worried: instead, the company is now focusing on converting those with active accounts into more viable customers.

Elsewhere in the results, we heard from Sony CFO Lin Tao that the PlayStation 6 is on track and "progressing as scheduled", with "solid progress" expected on the machine in 2027. Regarding those falling PS5 sales, Tao also referenced that, and says it's all part of the natural cycle of console launches and iteration. "Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform."

It must be encouraging for Sony to see this growth in this quarter, especially after all the bad press and furore around the company's decision to end the manufacturing of PlayStation discs by January 2028. It seems to be a core part of the gaming audience's understanding of game ownership, the decision has been widely contested as anti-consumer. It's caused a lot of bad blood with PlayStation players over the past six months, but - seemingly, given these results - that has translated to very little material impact on Sony's bottom line.

Reader, a confession: each night, before I retire to my chambers, I light a small votive candle. Bowing over it, I clasp my hands and beseech the ghost of Josh Sawyer (who is not dead) to return to the Pillars of Eternity games and add the weirdly-decent gamepad support they got on console to their PC iterations. I am an old man who wants to play them on my Steam Deck, and the existing Steam Input templates don't cut it for me.

My prayers are answered. In an announcement yesterday, Obsidian declared that now is the time of the Pillars of Eternity and Deadfire: Controller Support Public Test. Both PoE 1 and 2 have ongoing Steam betas that will allow you to play with full, start-to-finish controller support. You can opt into them and try the new feature for yourself by visiting each game's properties and opting into their respective November 4 beta versions.

Being betas, they're a touch buggy right now. Indeed, one of Obsidian's very first notices to players in the public test's announcement is "This is a public test, so please expect bugs", but I'm nevertheless impressed by the limited time I've spent mucking around with the games on Steam Deck.

There are a couple of misaligned gamepad prompts, and a very slight amount of awkwardness with the analogue movement, but frankly my main takeaway is 'Dang, it's kind of wild how well these isometric CRPGs adjust to non-keyboard-and-mouse support'. Which, yeah, is how I felt about the console versions too.

The public test runs until November 25, and the devs will use the data gathered to iron out wrinkles like those I just listed for a full release.

It's not all about gamepad support, by the way. Just, you know, mostly. Obsidian also announced patch 1.3.10.0 for PoE 1 and patch 5.1.0.0 for Deadfire. In PoE 1's case, the patch mostly smooths out some minor niggling bugs with the UI and the game's recently implemented turn-based mode.

Deadfire's patch is meatier: that game's older turn-based mode has been rejigged to integrate the improvements from PoE 1's turn-based mode. Characters no longer take a single turn per round (instead, they move as much as their initiative allows), lethality has been greatly increased—that kinda thing.

#3732. Nintendo game sales surge thanks to Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream, but Switch 2 hardware suffers big decline

Nintendo's latest financial earnings report is here, revealing healthy software sales thanks to the enormously popular Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream. Sales of Switch 2 hardware, however, are down.

As per Nintendo's 2nd Quarter fiscal earnings report, focusing on the three-month period ending 30th September 2026, Switch 2 hardware registered a big drop in sales during the first half of the current financial year (FY27).

Over that period, Nintendo sold 6.49m Switch 2 units and 1.27m units of the original Switch - equating to a 37.4 percent decline for Switch 2 and 32.7 percent decline for Switch 1 compared to the same period last year. Nintendo had previously forecast a decline in hardware sales, and the company still expects to sell 16.50m Switch 2 units by the end of the current fiscal year.

Nintendo software sales, on the other hand, saw a big year-on-year boost of 18.8 percent on Switch 2 (to 24.49m units) and a smaller increase of 6.8 percent on Switch 1. That's all thanks to the release of several popular first- and third-party titles over the first half of FY27. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream was by far the most successful game with 8.81m units sold, followed by Rhythm Heaven Groove at 2.89m. Splatoon Raiders (the only Switch 2 exclusive of the three) sold 2.42m. Nintendo also highlighted a 60.5 percent year-on-year increase in digital game sales.

The increase in software unit sales and the "continued weakness of the Yen" couldn't prevent the overall business from declining by 15.3 percent year-on-year, however.

Other remaining releases in Nintendo' s current fiscal year include The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake (which launches today and was awarded five stars in Eurogamer's review), Switch 2 re-releases of Pikmin 2 and Xenoblade Chronicles 3, as well as Metroid Ravenous, which arrives early in 2027.

#3731. 5 Tips To Make Sure You Have A Fun Time With Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse

The great thing about Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is that it’s a rat’s nest of puzzles, hidden rooms, and platforming challenges that’s actually enjoyable to sit down and untangle. There’s no puzzle or secret so esoteric as to be utterly confounding, but nor is it too simple. Pay enough attention, and you’ll never need a guide to get you through. However! We all could use a little help now and again to traverse the game’s rougher edges. I’ve got five tips for you that’ll make your time with Belmont’s Curse that much more enjoyable.

Through gameplay settings, developer Evil Empire has built into the game the ability for anyone, regardless of skill level, to enjoy it. And while I understand that for a very specific kind of gamer, the use of such settings is anathema, they really can be a boon. You don’t have to simply turn off deathâwhich you can doâyou can also tweak how much damage Rose takes or deals out. Increasing Rose’s experience gains can make her get stronger, faster if combat is an issue. You can choose the option to respawn outside of a boss door to cut down on runback fatigue. If traps like spike pits are messing you up as you try to tackle the game’s tricky platforming challenges, you can adjust how much damage you take from them. Even adjusting your standard allotment of healing potions can be enough to offset any difficulties you might have without bruising the ego too much.

There is so much communicated with your map beyond simply where you are in the world. Paying attention to a room’s color can let you know if you’re missing a secretâa brown background represents a completed room, a purple one still has something not yet discovered. In places like Dracula’s Castle and Notre Dame, the map will render important rooms with specific detail and can provide puzzle hints if you pay close attention. For example, it’ll tell you how many chains you need to break for the Sage and the general direction of where to find them. Use those map markers, too. You get 50 of them to place anywhere you want to make it easy to backtrack or mark things you haven’t discovered a use for yet.

Belmont’s Curse is stuffed with unique weapons, and among the seven types of armaments is bound to be one that’ll suit your play style. But while some of the weapons you find pack a decent punch, Rose’s tarot cards are where your true offensive and defensive capabilities are unlocked. Each boss you defeat grants you a new spell and, if you complete the little side-quests called Works of Mercy associated with each one, you can make them stronger. Upgrading your spells via Works of Mercy is akin to unlocking easy mode. The spells are so damn powerful that, when combined with a high-enough level for Rose, you can make many boss fights trivial. My favorite is the spell earned from the Brittle King. Fully upgrading it not only makes Rose nigh unkillable, it also adds a bit of extra damage oomph that has saved my ass in combat arenas more than once. And! A lot of the Works are simple enough to complete. Killing 25 haunted armor enemies is one Work of Mercy you can complete for the Brittle King, and you’ve already done that several times over in the time it takes to get to him.

I’ve already mentioned this elsewhere, but the mirrors are more than just save points and the game isn’t the greatest about telling you that. This is another one of those “pay close attention for a neat reward” things, but kneeling in front of one (after unlocking Dracula’s Castle) will unlock fast travel. Kneeling teleports you to a hidden area home to (almost) all of the mirrors you’ve unlocked in an area. Pick where you want to go and the mirror will get you there. The mirror world itself is a puzzle to be solved so I won’t spoil more, but until you’ve solved it, fast travel only works within a zone. You’ll have to rely on the Ferryman to travel between them.

This one is highly specific, but it is helpful for the middle of the game. After unlocking Dracula’s Castle, the next area you’ll delve into is Notre Dame. There, the final boss room is blocked off by three different lasers that you shut down one by one. There are also tons of secrets and challenges that make use of the lasers to increase their difficulty. Instead of trying to juggle laser beams sniping at you as you go for a chest hidden at the end of a dangerous room, focus on defeating the boss as soon as possible, then go back and try the challenges you missed in the old church. Turning off the lasers guarding the boss door turns them off everywhere else, making a lot of Notre Dame’s platforming challenges much easier.

#3728. Mass Effect petition has enough signatures for the Canadian Government to potentially save BioWare

Following news of EA's decision to shut down iconic RPG studio BioWare, Canadian fans of the studio have escalated their grievances to the governmental level, calling on the Canadian Government to step in and save the Canadian studio from closure, seemingly after Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis called on the government to do so.

Fans have submitted a petition to the Canadian House of Commons arguing for the government to find a way for BioWare to continue, such as through funding that allows the studio to buy the Mass Effect and other IPs and go independent.

The petition, number e-7898, argues that "BioWare is one of Canada's most important cultural exports" and that the studio's closure by its American parent company "represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy."

"BioWare's productions champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights that are at the centre of Canada's national identity," it continued.

The petition opened for signatures on 4th of November, and has already amassed 1,700 signatures. By law, petitions that surpass 500 valid signatures from Canadian citizens or residents are entered into the House of Commons' agenda, meaning they will be presented in front of the parliament.

As encouraging as that may be, it's worth keeping in mind that it may not result in meaningful change. Even if the Canadian Government agrees with the petition's goals, it cannot force EA to sell BioWare or its various IPs.

EA notably didn't shop the studio around before closing it down, and the publisher has a history of closing down owned studios rather than selling them off. EA has also kept the IPs of its various shuttered studios.

The community's reaction to BioWare's closure has taken different forms. Hundreds of thousands signed a different petition to save Mass Effect. The people behind the movement have purchased billboards in Times Square in New York City to advertise it, with plans for more outside The Game Awards ceremony in December.

Meanwhile, former BioWare developers have spoken about the last days of BioWare, and the work they've poured into Mass Effect Universe, the studio's final project before it was shuttered.

Grey's Anatomy is one of the most legendary medical dramas of all time, and we're currently in its whopping 23rd season on ABC (and streaming with a Hulu subscription). The beloved medical drama is till going strong, but many fans like to look back at its glory days. Late actor Eric Dane famously played Mark Sloane/ McSteamy during that time, and excerpts from his posthumous memoir got honest about his struggles during that time.

McSteamy is one of the most beloved Grey's character of all time, in no small part thanks to the charisma and heart that Dane brought to the role. In his recently released memoir My Book of Days (via EW) he wrote about an injury and reliance on painkillers resulted in him deteriorating during his time at Seattle Grace Hospital. He wrote:

My body goes to shit. I drop to 170, my face caves in, my eyes cloud, I look gaunt; shit, I look like a drug addict. You can tell. I can tell. My attitude on set changes. I’m no longer bubbly, the fun guy, a ringleader in laughs. I don’t act out. I don’t throw tantrums or chairs. I go the other way. I bring everything inside. I dissolve.

What a heartbreaking recollection. While Grey's fans were still head over heels in love with Sloan, Dane was having a private struggle with his health and substances that was making his job difficult. Rather than acting out he felt himself "dissolving", and not letting it impact this coworkers. Indeed, Grey's Anatomy stars wrote tributes to the late actor following his tragic death in February.

Later in his memoir, the Euphoria star does mention that his coworkers noticed the change in him. He wrote about the dynamic he felt at the time, in a section which reads:

I can’t help it. I feel other members of the cast looking at me. They’re my friends. My work family. No. My family. They don’t judge me. They don’t look angry. They look concerned. They look sad.

It's tough to hear how Eric Dane was struggling during this time, and how he was being so private about it while bringing McSteamy to life. He didn't want to bother his co-workers and chosen family, but they noticed that something was going on. That includes the one and only Shonda Rhimes, who did offer to help the Last Ship actor. As he wrote:

I tell her I’m dealing with it. I lie to her. I lie to myself. I suck it up. Fight through it. I don’t want to be Shonda’s burden. I don’t want to be a problem. But I am. I am a problem.

Clearly Eric Dane took the time to reflect on his years on Grey's Anatomy, and the struggles he was dealing with at the time. In his book he was able to speak honestly about his issues, and take responsibility for being a "problem." It's a powerful testament, one that might help inspire readers who are dealing with similar issues.

New episodes of Grey's Anatomy air Thursdays on ABC as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Folks who want to re-watch Dane's iconic tenure as McSteamy can do so on both Hulu and Netflix. Although after hearing about his experience, it might hit differently.

#3726. Final Fantasy 10 Blitzball Was Inspired By Star Wars Podracing

Final Fantasy has a lot of minigames but few are as bizarre and as beloved as Blitzball, a version of underwater soccer invented for Final Fantasy X. That game’s director and producer, Square Enix veteran Yoshinori Kitase, recently revealed one of the inspirations for the fictional sport: Star Wars.

Blitzball is played in a giant sphere of water that hovers in the air. It’s like a combination of soccer and rugby, with players ramming into each other and doing special kick moves to try to score points by knocking the ball into a high-tech backboard.

Unlike most Final Fantasy minigames, Blitzball plays a major role in FFX‘s story. In addition to being the backdrop for the game’s stunning FMV cutscene intro, it’s also the main vocation of the central protagonist, Titus. NPCs you meet out in the world can be recruited to play on your team, and finishing at the top of the league is required to unlock a special late-game item.

So how did Kitase come up with it? He was talking about how Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took inspiration from Final Fantasy when he mentioned that his own work on the franchise was inspired in part by things like Star Wars.

“One more [example of a Star Wars influence in FF] that came to my mind is from Final Fantasy X, where I had to create [Blitzball] for the game inside the fantasy setting,” he told IGN at the Lucca Comics & Games Festival 2026. “And I used an idea from Star Wars Episode I where there’s this [pod]race and the fact of using sport inside a fantasy context, I took this idea directly from Star Wars.”

Star Wars creator George Lucas’ own idea for podracing grew out of his love of car racing and hot rod culture. Little did he know it would help spawn a completely different fictional sport in a completely different universe. Weirdly enough, Blitzball has been mentioned in the Star Wars galaxy before.

Author Mike Chen namedropped it in his Star Wars novel Brotherhood. Confirming that it was a deliberate reference to Final Fantasy and not just a name he came up with independently, back in 2022 he tweeted, “Blitzball is basically underwater hockey played as a minigame in Final Fantasy X. As a former NHL writer, I freaking loved Blitzball and spent hours winning leagues.”

#3725. Jen Affleck Files for Divorce From Zac While Pregnant With Baby No. 4

Jen Affleck has reportedly filed for divorce from her husband, Zac Affleck, just days before The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County premieres.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Jen, 27, reportedly filed a Tuesday, November 3, petition for divorce in Utah, where the pair wed. The Hulu reality star also submitted a proposed parenting plan, though the details of the filing are private.

The court records do not reveal the reason behind the breakup or Jen’s requested custody arrangements.

Us has reached out to reps for Jen and Zac, 30, for comment.

The couple — who announced in June that they are expecting baby No. 4 — met on the Mormon dating app Mutual in 2018 before getting engaged. They ultimately got married in 2019.

Jen and Zac’s love story was first put on display for the world to see when The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives premiered in September 2024. Since then, Hulu cameras have documented the pair struggling to keep their marriage strong and healthy.

Starting November 12, viewers will get another front-row seat into the state of their relationship when Jen appears on the spinoff show, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.

“We were so vulnerable, and we shared everything about our religion and our life and our marriage,” Zac said on a May 2025 episode of “The Viall Files” podcast. “I honestly think we went a little bit naive into the show — just not really knowing what to expect or what reality TV even is.”

Jen, however, always viewed reality TV as a way to confront life’s problems and make a change for the better.

“Sometimes you just feel called to something and you can’t explain why,” she detailed. “It’s not easy being vulnerable as a Mormon and showing what actually happens sometimes in Mormon relationships. I feel like we’re doing the hard thing but doing the right thing by exposing what actually happens.”

In a recent interview with People, Jen admitted that her marriage wasn’t as strong as she had hoped. At the same time, she remained hopeful that better days were ahead as she got used to life in Southern California.

“It’s been a lot the past couple of months, I’ll be honest,” Jen revealed to the publication in August. “But I do feel like I’m seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and just trying to count my blessings every single day.”

The Switch 2 is still comfortably ahead of the Switch in its first year, but it might not be ahead by its second.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Switch 2 sales have plummeted over the summer months compared to this time last year; accounting for a drop of nearly four million units. That's sure to be a warning sign for Nintendo, especially as the company increased the price for the handheld across the globe at the start of September—near the end of the period it's currently reporting—which could have an impact on future sales over the busy holiday period.

Nintendo has reported its sales figures from April 1, 2026 until September 30, 2026. It calls this period 'FY27 Q1-Q2' because companies are weird. Nevertheless, it's the previous six months of the year, and it's been a tough one for hardware.

The Switch 2 sold 6.49 million units: a 3.87 million unit reduction compared to the 10.36 million in the same period last year. That makes a change from the original Switch, which sold in increasingly larger amounts for the first five years of its life.

The Switch sold just 1.27 million units during the same period, down 32.7%, but that's not a huge surprise for the outgoing handheld.

So, what to make of the dip? It is a marked reduction in Switch 2 sales compared to its bumper launch year. But that's the thing. The Switch 2 sold incredibly well in its first year; 19.8 million units sold. That's a bigger success story than the Switch. It launched just before the end of Nintendo's weird financial years but reached around 17.7 million units sold by the end of its first full year. Though it did go on to double that figure the following year, which the Switch 2 is likely to fail to achieve.

Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 over the course of this summer period. It first announced the price increase in May, 2026; however, it didn't implement it until September 1, 2026 in most of the affected regions (US, Canada, Europe). Only Japan saw a sudden price increase effective in May, 2026.

The company asks $500 for the console, an increase of $50 over its original launch price. It blamed "changes in market conditions" at the time, which is common parlance for 'memory prices are ruining everything.'

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

The most recent reporting period ended on September 30. So we don't quite know what impact that $50 price hike will have on the success of the handheld from these figures alone; however, Nintendo has reevaluated its forecast up until March 31, 2027 at just 16.5 million Switch 2 units sold; down from 19.86 million in the previous 12-month period. That's a 16.9% reduction.

"Although unit sales of Nintendo Switch 2 hardware declined compared to the same period of last fiscal year, many consumers continued to adopt the system, spurred on by factors like the release of new titles," Nintendo says.

And it's true, games are flying off the shelves for the Switch 2 relative to last year. Up 18.8%, from 20.62 million to 24.49 million. A certain remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time might help bump those figures, with the game coming out today. Even Switch titles are selling like hot cakes; the majority of game sales remain with the bulk of players on the last-gen console. Up 6.8%, from 61.56 million to 65.73 million.

So it's not all bad for Nintendo—it still has one of the best-selling consoles on its hands. It's just been curtailed by the pesky memory and cost of living crises. Haven't we all?

Since Patrick Stewart's death became public knowledge nearly a week ago, many across social media have been taking the time to honor the late actor. Also, a number celebrities have been honoring Stewart, including more than a few of his Star Trek cohorts. On that note, John de Lancie is now adding his voice to the many who've been sharing their memories of the Jean-Luc Picard portrayer. The beloved Q actor paid a fitting tribute to his former co-star and dropped the perfect reference tied to Picard and Q's past tussles.

While he wasn't a main character, John de Lancie's Q became one of Star Trek: The Next Generation's most memorable foes. After many adventures over the years, including Picard, De Lancie posted the following message about Stewart on Facebook:

For forty years, Q has been a thorn in Jean-Luc Picard’s side. And what a pleasure it has been to be that thorn. Patrick Stewart was a wonderful actor. He brought intelligence and depth to every role he played. It was a privilege to have worked with him. The universe is a little smaller and a little less bright today with his passing. Goodbye, Patrick. You touched so many. See you out there, Mon Capitaine.

That "mon Capitaine" brought a tear to my eye when I read it, and reminded me of some of my favorite TNG episodes. While Q and Picard's relationship ran hot and cold, I could always sense that it was always love coming from the former's end. Of course, he was certainly a jerk, putting Picard through some wtf-worthy scenarios, but I always appreciated that there was some mutual love between them at the end of Picard's second season.

I'm A Star Trek Fan, But I'd Never Heard This Cool Story About Patrick Stewart Showing Up On Jeremy Clarkson's Set

For those who haven't streamed Picard Season 2 with a Paramount+ subscription, the storyline ends with Picard's realization that Q has constructed the entire scenario he's put them through in order to help him overcome past trauma. Q then reveals to Picard that he is dying, and the two share a hug before Q sets the timeline right again.

It was emotional for me, even if it was potentially retconned when Picard Season 3 had Q return in a post-credits scene. Fans have, however, theorized that everything from the Q species exists outside of time. Therefore, his death doesn't have to be linear.

Personally, I think Q is not above faking his own death just for the thrill of pulling one over on Picard. The fact of the matter is, we'll likely never know now that Patrick Stewart is gone, though I'm sure he won't be the last to play Picard. Star Trek hasn't been afraid to recast iconic characters, though I think it'll be a challenge for someone to follow in Stewart's footsteps and play the role.

Patrick Stewart's death comes amid the celebration of Star Trek's 60th anniversary, which has been rife with bad news. As far as the franchise itself goes, there is a movie in development, but no TV shows are actively in the works as far as the general public knows. Stewart's passing certainly feels like a gut punch to the fandom and the former actors, many of whom held out hope for positive news before the year's end.

Tributes continue to pour in for Patrick Stewart, and I'm continuing to love every eulogy and story that is shared. Both Star Trek: The Next Generation and Picard are available to stream on Paramount+, so anyone who is missing the great Captain should head over there and watch some classic episodes.

#3722. Mass Effect Fans Get Enough Signatures To Plead To The Canadian Government For BioWare’s Life

In the two weeks since the closure of BioWare,Â fans of the Canadian RPG studio have been rallying around different petitions and causes, whether they be advocating for the revival of the studio’s canceledÂ Mass Effect: Universe or asking publisher Electronic Arts to give the IP to a new studio that could make games in its sci-fi universe instead. However, following calls from Canadian politician Avi Lewis for the government to help assist BioWare workers in buying the studio and going independent, fans have put together a petition to bring the notion to the Canadian House of Commons, and they’ve already received enough signatures to do so.

The petition, sponsored by Parliament member Don Davies, argues that BioWare is one of Canada’s “most important cultural exports” and that the shuttering by American parent company Electronic Arts “represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada’s cultural legacy.”

We, the undersigned, citizens and residents of Canada, call upon the Government of Canada to:

1. Provide BioWare with the capital necessary to secure independence of themselves and their intellectual property from Electronic Arts and resume business as an independent, Canadian company;

2. Protect Canadian businesses and cultural institutions from being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests; and

3. Champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada’s national identity by preserving BioWare’s invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry.

As laid out on the House of Commons website, petitions like these require 500 validated signatures from Canadian citizens, presumably so they can’t be spammed by people outside of the country who support a cause, and it has surpassed that number. This means that it will be presented or tabled in the House of Commons, so there will be some kind of official response to this petition.

It’s worth noting that, regardless of what the Canadian government decides to do here, EA still owns BioWare and its IP, so it would require the company’s cooperation and approval. EA historically doesn’t sell its IP or studios, which many assume is why it didn’t sell off BioWare following its acquisition by private equity earlier this year, so don’t get your hopes up just yet.

Reports that followed BioWare’s closure claim that EA decided to shutter the studio and cancel Mass Effect: UniverseÂ after weighing its budget and choosing to prioritizeÂ Star Wars: Battlefront 3, a game that it reportedly hasn’t begun actual development on, over BioWare’s sci-fi RPG sequel.

Viewers have a lot of opinions about Jen Affleck and Zac Affleck‘s marriage after watching their relationship play out on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives.

The couple started dating in 2018 and got married one year later. After expanding their family twice, Jen and Zac joined the cast of Hulu’s reality series The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, which followed a group of Mormon mom influencers in Utah. Season 1 showed Jen and Zac nearly calling it quits before admitting they were still a work in progress.

“Ever since we finished filming, we’ve been doing nonstop therapy and it’s been great,” Jen exclusively told Us Weekly in September 2024 after the series premiered. “So if anything, [watching the show] is just going to be exposure therapy at this point. We’ve healed and now we’re ready to talk about it once it comes out.”

Jen also denied that her husband had anything to do with her leaving MomTok, saying, “It had a lot to do with just me and just figuring out everything. There are so many factors — not just our relationship — like religion, friendships and my children.”

She continued: “In order to make the right decision for me and my family, I really had to take a step back and ask myself, ‘How am I going to move forward and what’s best for us?’ You’ll just have to wait for season 2 to see what happens.”

That same month, Jen praised Zac for how he supported her — emotionally and monetarily — since they started dating.

“Zac bought me my first laptop when he had $10 in his bank account. When I shared my dream of running a marathon, he trained alongside me and ran it with me. I told him I wanted to start my videography business, so he saved up money and bought me my first camera. When we were expecting our first baby, I wanted a place to call home, so he worked hard, saved up, and bought us our first house,” she wrote via Instagram at the time. “He gave me both stability and freedom, which allowed me to post videos online and launch my career on social media. This, in turn allowed me to support him and our family while he’s been in school.”

Jen noted she “couldn’t have” found success on her own without Zac by her side.

“Is Zac perfect? No. Does he have flaws that we’ve needed to address? Yes. But I can confidently say he’s always supported and believed in me more than anyone else,” she continued. “We’re still young, we have two precious babies, and we still have struggles like so many marriages. But do we love each other? Yes. Are we willing to put in the work to be better? Yes. Have there been moments when we wanted to walk away? Of course. But there’s so much more to our marriage and what we offer to each other than people realize.”

After Hulu renewed The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives for season 2, viewers questioned the status of Jen and Zac’s marriage. The pair took a step back from sharing highlights from their relationship once they made the move from Utah to New York so Zac could attend medical school.

Keep scrolling to relive Jen and Zac’s relationship before — and after — The Secret Wives of Mormon Wives:

Jen and Zac started dating in 2018 after meeting on Mormon dating app Mutual. After one year of dating, Zac proposed at Top of the Rock in New York City.

The duo tied the knot in 2019 at a local The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints temple.

“I knew Zac was the one when I realized I couldn’t imagine life without him & his amazing qualities,” Jen wrote via Instagram ahead of their wedding ceremony. “I’m grateful to have someone who loves me unconditionally, puts me first, & makes me want to be a better fiancé, friend, daughter and person. Can’t forget he makes me the happiest girl alive.”

Zac and Jen welcomed their first child, daughter Nora, in November 2021. The reality star reflected on the milestone moment three years later, writing via Instagram, “Nora brings so much joy and light into our lives, and I feel incredibly blessed to be her mom 🥺 There are countless things that I adore about her — she’s spunky, kind, and full of life. … To us, she truly is everything.”

“Three years ago today I made the best decision of my life. That was to marry my best friend. It was a day we’ll always remember,” Jen gushed on social media. “To be surrounded by everyone we love, promising each other the world, we were so excited to start this new adventure. I wish I could relive every second of this day. It truly was a DREAM.”

Jen and Zac’s son, Lucas, was born in July 2023.

“We were so young when we first became parents, with lots to learn, but Zac has always been there every step of the way,” Jen wrote via Instagram in honor of Father’s Day in 2024. “He’s never wavered in giving Nora and Luca everything they need.”

Zac and Jennifer weathered some public storms when season 1 of The Secret Wives of Mormon Wives premiered on Hulu. Initially, Jen was presented as a more conservative Mormon, but it wasn’t until the end of the season that her costars — and viewers — got a glimpse at her marital issues when Zac told her she had “no values or morals” for enjoying a girls’ night out in Las Vegas.

Jen’s costar Demi Engemann claimed she saw text messages in which Zac threatened to end their marriage, said he didn’t love her anymore and made his wife come to his hotel room in the middle of the night to work out their problems. Demi also accused Zac of having a gambling problem, which is forbidden by the Mormon church.

“I think that there was a lot of things that Jen was doing at the time — and I think she would admit this — that were kind of driven by Zac’s insecurities,” Demi told Us at the time “I really do feel like she has found her voice. She’s now, like, ‘Hey, we are individuals as well as a couple. I have every right to do what feels right for me too within certain boundaries and respect for the relationship.’ But I think she has found her voice and I’m excited to see how that dynamic shifts.”

Costar Jessi Ngatikaura, meanwhile, questioned “the influence” Zac had on Jennifer.

“He’s the man of the house and has a lot of opinions on things,” Jessi noted to Us. “So I don’t think Jen would ever make that decision [to leave] on her own because she loves the friend group and she loves being around us. I would say that he definitely has a lot of influence on her decisions.”

The pair didn’t just make headlines because of their rocky marriage. After Zac claimed on screen that he was actor Ben Affleck‘s second cousin, fans and costars alike questioned the validity of that connection.

“I don’t think Jen would lie about that. I really don’t, but maybe [Zac] could. I mean, we’ve seen a little bit of how he can be,” Jessi said on Scheana Shay’s “Scheananigans” podcast. “But also maybe Ben Affleck’s team’s like, ‘We want nothing to do with you guys.’ So let’s dig and, like, plant this story because Zac is looking a little bad.”

Jessi noted that Jen and Zac “made the last name such a thing.” Reports later surfaced that Jen and Zac are not related to Ben, which they have not addressed. Jen previously told Us that she never crossed paths with Ben.

“We’ve never met him,” she said in September 2024. “Zac’s dad has, a long time ago. Hopefully we meet him sometime soon because we are family.”

Despite social media backlash about her marriage, Jen stood by Zac.

“I definitely think it was the best thing to happen to our relationship. While watching the show, a lot of people are going to think that maybe this would break our relationship apart. But if anything, it did the opposite,” Jen explained to Us when asked how the show impacted her marriage. “Being on camera and having those moments happen made us take a step back and actually look at a relationship and make us just see what we have to change.”

Jen took to Instagram to share a message reflecting on the highlights from her relationship with Zac.

“We were just kids when we got married. Young, naive, and inexperienced, we truly had no idea what we were getting ourselves into. Coming from completely different backgrounds, families, and upbringings, it didn’t seem to make sense. We were polar opposites,” she captioned the post. “How could we make this work? How could we see the same picture?”

Jen admitted that the twosome aren’t always on the same page, adding, “We didn’t always see eye to eye, and a lot of times, we still don’t. But that’s what marriage is, we keep trying. I truly believe there were lessons we both needed to teach each other.”

Jen sparked split speculation when she shared multiple TikTok videos that clearly showed her missing a ring on her left hand. Jen didn’t address the rumors but Zac was still featured in posts across her various social media platforms.

Hulu renewed The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives for a second season one month after the show premiered. Jen and Zac moved from Utah to New York once filming started, which left their status with the show unclear.

“Choosing to step away from social media has been one of the best things I’ve done for my mental health,” Jen wrote via Instagram Story. “I can’t lie — these months have been some of the toughest I’ve faced, but they’ve also helped me gain clarity about myself, my relationships and the mother and friend I aspire to be.”

Zac, meanwhile, kept his Instagram account private while his bio read, “Official Fan Page of Jen, Nora and Luca @jenniferlaffleck.”

Jen announced she is pregnant and expecting her third baby with Zac later this year.

“I’ve always dreamed of a big family, and seeing that dream come true is both exciting and fulfilling,” Jen shared with People. “It can be daunting to think about raising three babies while pursuing my career, but I want to show women and mothers that they can achieve anything they set their minds to, no matter how unrealistic it may seem.”

During an episode of “The Viall Files,” Jen and Zac first broke down what led them to reality TV — and revealed how the experience almost ruined their relationship.

“We were so vulnerable and we shared everything about our religion and our life and our marriage,” Zac said. “I honestly think we went a little bit naive into the show — just not really knowing what to expect or what reality TV even is.”

Jen, meanwhile, expressed hope that her involvement in the show would start a conversation. “Sometimes you just feel called to something and you can’t explain why,” she detailed. “It’s not easy being vulnerable as a Mormon and showing what actually happens sometimes in Mormon relationships. I feel like we’re doing the hard thing but doing the right thing by exposing what actually happens.”

She continued: “Hopefully people within the Mormon culture can look at our relationship and reflect on theirs and say like, ‘Hey, I think we kind of struggle with that too. Or maybe my husband has fed into the patriarchy and isn’t treating me right.’ I want to be an example of that. People aren’t going to like that, unfortunately.”

Elsewhere in the episode, Zac explained why he was surprised by Jen’s second pregnancy. “We had one and then a second baby back to back. Jen — like, six months after she gave birth — she got pregnant again with her second baby,” he said before claiming, “I got tricked into it. She took out her IUD without telling me.”

Zac called that period of time “stressful” and noted it was before they got into therapy. Jen, meanwhile, found the revelation about her second pregnancy more funny, adding, “Whoopsies, I forgot to tell you [I took my IUD out].”

“This year has tested us in ways I never imagined, yet somehow we found a way to come out stronger than before,” Jen wrote for her and Zac’s anniversary.

The couple welcomed their third baby, daughter Penelope, days later. “She is perfect,” Jen wrote via Instagram on Wednesday, July 2. “Going unmedicated was truly the most painful but empowering experience of my life. I could not have done it without Zac and my supportive doula! I’m so grateful and so happy that Penny is earth side now.”

Jen announced via Instagram that she and Zac are expecting their fourth baby.

“Chapter Four. 🤍,” she wrote alongside a photo of herself cradling her baby bump.

Five months after Jen announced her pregnancy with baby No. 4, TMZ reported that she filed for divorce from Zac. Us reached out to reps for the pair for comment.

With the Xbox Series X and S rapidly ageing, it looks unlikely that the next console generation will be affordable at all. As such, I've been looking at AMD to bring its modern GPU feature set to older hardware to stop me from having to upgrade. It seems it felt my gaze, and Xbox Series X, S, and Xbox handhelds now have FSR 4.1.2 support, which developers can turn on in their games.

AMD has just updated its Game Development Kit with FSR 4.1.2 and two new upscaling models for Xbox Series X and S: the Full INT8 model and the more efficient Lite INT8 model. The Lite one is half the size of the Full one and has a lower upscaling cost. Either console can use either model, but game developers are able to choose which type they implement.

AMD has put out a GDK sample for developers to test, which "switches between the Full and Lite models at runtime, so developers can compare image quality and upscaling cost in the same scene. Upscaler memory is the same for both models because it depends on render and display resolution, not on the model. That makes the choice a performance trade-off, not a memory one."

Interestingly, Ancient Gameplays tested the Lite and Full models two weeks ago and noticed that Lite works better with lower input resolution and even removes some visual noise that is kept in the Full model. They say the "Lite model needs to be more stable because it will be aimed at handheld devices, iGPUs from laptops, and the render resolution on those cases will be way, way lower."

FSR 4.1.2 is also now supported on Xbox handhelds (the top-end ROG Xbox Ally range to start with), though this is seemingly only the one "highly efficient INT8 model", and developers can only get access via Asus' preview driver for the Xbox Ally X and X20. AMD says "it upgrades DirectX 12 games with FSR 3.1 or newer, and ROG Xbox Ally support follows in a later update."

How developers choose to integrate FSR 4.1.2 on Xbox Series X and S will be on a case-by-case basis, but the Lite model being solid certainly suggests good things for future optimisations. And RX 6000 graphics cards got FSR 4.1 early, just a few weeks ago, giving older hardware a little bit more performance.

This is all just in time for a huge launch on Xbox: Grand Theft Auto 6. The game officially launches on November 19, and being a Rockstar game, it's looking like it will be a real graphical showcase. But playing on six-year-old hardware could pose a challenge, so getting an upscaling hand just before the game reaches the starting line surely can't hurt its reception. You won't be able to play the game on Xbox handhelds until the PC port (they aren't really Xbox consoles after all), but I won't be complaining when I'm squeezing a bit more performance out of my Z2 Extreme chip in everything else.

3. Best high performance: MSI Claw 8 EX AI+

It’s been a big year for Kelly Clarkson, one marked by considerable change for her. Back in August, viewers were treated to the final episode of The Kelly Clarkson Show, which wrapped up the talk show’s seven-season run. Clarkson has since partaken in other ventures, like returning to her coaching duties on The Voice. That aside, October proved to be a long month for her due to that controversy involving the mechanical bird. Now, though, I’m hoping Clarkson is celebrating some major news regarding her since-ended show.

Last week, the 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards were held, where various stars took home the coveted golden trophies for their work on the small screen. Clarkson’s eponymous chat show was among the programs in the mix, as it was nominated in 11 categories (which ensured it would go out with a bang). The show ultimately proved to have a great outing at this year’s ceremony, as it ended up winning five awards. Check out the specific categories below:

In snagging those five categories, the series managed to edge out long-running soap opera General Hospital, which took home four awards. As it stands, Kelly Clarkson’s show now has a total of 27 Daytime Emmys, which is incredibly impressive. It’s impressive to look at that from the larger perspective of the show’s run but, more immediately, it’s sweet to see the show bow out with several additional statues under its belt. The Outstanding Daytime Talk Series award is particularly impressive.

This award-heavy development is a stark contrast to the viral situation that Clarkson has been involved with over the past month. In recent weeks, the entertainer has been involved in a beef of sorts involving a novelty store, and it remains a topic of public discussion.

The $15,000 (Or $15 Million Bird) Is Way, Way In Demand After Kelly Clarkson Drama

In October, Clarkson took to social media to post about an experience she apparently had at Art of Play, a store located in Brooklyn. Clarkson claimed she’d been treated like Julia Roberts’ character from Pretty Woman, as she was apparently wanting to purchase a singing bird automaton. The store’s management team later responded to the claims, saying that they tried to explain to Clarkson that the bird was not for sale and used exclusively for in-store events. However, Clarkson seemed to counter that notion when she shared a photo of the bird with a $15,000 price tag.

Further updates have since cropped up regarding this situation, with the store’s security footage even being leaked by journalist Pablo Torre. AoP, which is owned by children' s book author Adam Rubin, has reportedly received backlash on social media, and patrons of the establishment have as well. While Clarkson allegedly believes she’s not at fault in the matter, insiders claim that those in her inner circle have been surprised by how this situation has escalated.

As of right now, it’s unclear whether or not Kelly Clarkson and Art of Play will come to any kind of understanding. In the meantime, though, Clarkson can celebrate her talk show being honored with a few more Emmys following its successful run.

#3718. Heidi Klum Shocks In Severed Hand Halloween Costume

Heidi Klum has done it again. The Project Runway host exceeded all our Halloween expectations by transforming herself into a giant, severed human hand nearly two meters tall for the latest edition of her annual party, held Saturday night in New York City. The costume, which required hours of work by her makeup and prop team, left no detail to chance: hyper-realistic veins modeled after her own anatomy, wrinkles, red-painted nails, and an exxagerated version of the rings she typically wears.

“Mike [Marino, from the special effects team ProRenFX] has all of these scans of my body, so he was able to use those to create an exact replica of my hand,” Klum explained to Vogue. “We wanted everything to be as realistic as possible—the anatomy, the veins, the muscles, all the little details that make a hand look like a real hand.”

The costume’s structure used the model's legs to form two of the fingers, while her right arm provided mobility for the thumb. Only her eyes and mouth were visible amid the bloody wounds on her palm, from which—to top off the gruesomeness of it all—Heidi Klum would occasionally spit out the fake blood that a team of assistants injected into her mouth. The most macabre part was at the wrist, where a horrific gash exposed a jumble of blood, bones, and torn flesh.

Heidi Klum (L) recieves an injection of fake blood to augment her 2026 Halloween costume.

Other guests at Klum's party included Kyle MacLachlan, who arrived dressed as his character from The Flintstones; Neil Patrick Harris and his husband David Burtka, dressed as the girls from The Shining; and Heidi Klum and Flavio Briatore's daughter, Leni Klum.

Before making her grand entrance, the host had built up anticipation on social media by posting clues about this year’s costume, such as a photo of her real hand that showed her wedding ring alongside the small tattoo of husband Tom Kaulitz's name. It, too, was part of her Halloween costume. “Nothing was overlooked! I love that Mike pays attention to things that most people might not even notice at first. The details make these costumes so special. It’s not just any giant hand: It’s my giant hand!” Klum said.

Heidi Klum 2026 Halloween costume, as seen from the back.

This is the 25th annual Halloween party thrown by the former Victoria’s Secret Angel: The event began in 2000, and has only continued to expand in scope. “ “Can you believe it? Twenty-five years of Halloween, costumes, incredible transformations, and so many amazing memories,” she said.

Last night’s “amputated hand” joins Klum's collection of Halloween costumes that ranges from last year’s mythological Medusa (with a petrified Kaulitz by her side) to E.T., to Shrek’s Fiona, to a disgusting giant worm inside which she feared she might suffocate. We're already looking forward to what she comes up with for next year.

#3717. 'Mormon Wives' Couples Who've Split, Divorced Since Appearing on the Show

The cast of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives has become synonymous with messy breakups, and the drama hasn’t stayed on screen.

Since the Hulu series debuted in 2024, multiple MomTok stars have seen their marriages and relationships unravel in very public ways — complete with divorce filings, custody battles, cheating allegations and tearful TikTok confessionals.

From finalized divorces to ongoing separations, scroll below to see which Mormon Wives couples have called it quits since the series’ premiere:

Jordan Ngatikaura filed for divorce from Jessi Draper in March 2026, months after her emotional cheating scandal with fellow Hulu star Marciano Brunette while filming Vanderpump Villa.

Jessi and Jordan, who share son Jagger and daughter Jovi, signed off on their divorce paperwork in September 2026, closing the book on five years of marriage.

“Now that our divorce has been signed, I’m grateful to have some closure and the opportunity to move forward,” Jordan told Us in a statement. “Jessi and I shared a meaningful chapter of our lives together, and no matter how that chapter ended, I will always be grateful for the good that came from it — especially our children.”

Jessi has since confirmed she’s dating Marciano, who is expected to play a larger role on Mormon Wives season 6.

Taylor Frankie Paul and Dakota Mortensen’s on-again, off-again relationship exploded into a custody war in 2026. The exes, who welcomed son Ever in March 2024, split for good in fall 2025 before Taylor filmed The Bachelorette season 22. (Taylor’s season was scrapped by ABC over resurfaced footage from her 2023 arrest.)

In March 2026, Dakota filed a temporary restraining order, alleging Taylor choked him and shoved him into a window during a February altercation. A judge granted him temporary sole custody of Ever.

Taylor, who denied the accusations, and Dakota were each issued mutual protective orders. She also received visitation rights of Ever. (Taylor also shares two older children with her ex-husband, Tate Paul, with whom she’s also been in a custody battle since June 2026.)

Layla Taylor tearfully confirmed her breakup from boyfriend Mason McWhorter in February 2026 after seven months of dating, insisting via social media there was “no bad blood” between them.

“I genuinely wish and want the best for Mason. Things just weren’t working out,” Layla explained. “I think we were just on two different paths right now. He felt in order for him to grow, he had to be on his own. I just really thought that I was gonna get the family that I wanted so badly.

Layla, who shares two sons with her ex-husband, later publicly came out as bisexual and is now dating Kelsie Chesser.

Mikayla Matthews and husband Jace Terry are still figuring things out after separating on Mormon Wives season 4, which premiered in March 2026.

“I think it’s tricky in this environment, because I also need a lot of support from him going through all of it,” Mikayla exclusively told Us. “It’s kind of one of those things that we’re still navigating, and it still has its ups and still has its downs.”

Season 3 saw the couple, who share four children, open up about intimacy issues that remained unresolved in season 4. Newly postpartum and battling chronic illness, Mikayla was shown packing up her belongings from their home.

“Unfortunately for me, it’s like I’m stuck in this place where my health is out of my control,” she explained. “I think it’s something we’re still working through, and we’re still going to be working through for a while.”

Jen Affleck reportedly filed for divorce from husband Zac Affleck in November 2026, just days before her The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County premiere.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Jen filed a petition for divorce in Utah. Jen, who is pregnant with baby No. 4, also submitted a proposed parenting plan.
